News.title: Tanker owners sued for $1m over terrifying cruise ship collision which left passengers stranded in water after capsizing
News.content:
Next

THE owners of a tanker that crashed into a cruise ship docked in New Orleans on Friday are being sued by port authorities.

Nearly 200 passengers on board survived the Mississippi River horror which caused more than $1million (£756k) in damages.



The port is now claiming the M/V Atlantic Asphalt is at fault for the disastrous smash, according to court documents.

A total of 32 people were treated at local hospitals following the catastrophe, but none had critical injuries.



All 197 passengers and crew on the American Heritage cruise ship survived as well as the employees aboard the tanker.

Officials called the dramatic rescue a “miracle on the Mississippi”.

The exact reason for the crash remains unknown, but US Coast Guard Captain Melanie Burnham said the tanker appears to have had “some type of a loss of steering”.

The National Transportation Safety Board has launched an investigation into the capsize.



Terrifying clips showed passengers clinging to the sides of the partially submerged ship and being pulled from the water in a frantic rescue.

Court documents allege the port terminal “was significantly damaged” in the ordeal.

The M/V Atlantic Asphalt, its owner Nave Shipping SA, and its management company, Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd, are all named in a federal court lawsuit filed on Friday in Louisiana.



Records show the port is demanding money to cover cleanup, inspections, repairs and other expenses.

The lawsuit also suggests the tanker should be seized and sold to pay for the damage.

It claims the collision “occurred as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness” of the ship and its operating companies.

The lawsuit alleges that the tanker and companies failed “to use all available means to avoid the risk” of ramming the riverboat.

In shocking footage of the incident, the huge tanker is seen steaming towards a smaller river cruiser as bystanders watch on in horror.



The huge Atlantic Asphalt slams straight into the side of the docked cruiser, reportedly punching a hole that pierced through to the ship’s dining room.

Emergency services rushed to the scene of the horror collision near the Port of New Orleans in Louisiana at around 12.30pm on Friday.

The ship tilts at a sharp angle and can be seen sinking rapidly.

It then falls fully on its side just feet from the port as rescuers scramble to save passengers from the river.

Passengers can be seen clinging to life rafts and attempting to swim to safety as their huge vessel begins to slip beneath the waves.



Footage recorded inside the river cruiser from the moments before the disaster shows the huge tanker heading straight for the smaller ship.

The passenger recording the video backs away from the window in fear before running for her life.

The Atlantic Asphalt capsized the American Heritage, a river cruise ship operated by American Cruise Lines.

Cruise ship restaurant manager Zayvion told ABC passengers were “scared” during “chaotic” scenes after the crash.

He said: “There was a hole in the hull of the other boat in the dining room.”



“It was a little chaotic, but our team knew what we were doing.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Zayvion added: “A lot of people were just scared, especially as the boat tipped over.

“It was scary for a lot of people. Even me, like, when it was tipping, I was like, it was getting real.”

News.title: Sprawling 19th century farmhouse to be knocked down TODAY after planners ruled it was illegally built on green belt land
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

FEELING GREEN Sprawling 19th century farmhouse to be knocked down TODAY after planners ruled it was illegally built on green belt land







Next

A SPRAWLING farmhouse is set to be demolished today after planners ruled it was illegally built on green belt land.

The charming 19th century property on Dones View Farm in Dutton, Cheshire, will be knocked down at a cost of £20,000.



Retired builder Barry Devine bought the barn in 2000 and spent 19 years transforming the pad into a substantial house with separate wings.

Mr Devine claims he never needed planning permission, but council planners argued it’s an entirely new house and ordered its demolition in 2019.



Cheshire West and Chester Council also demanded the removal of boundary walls and fencing.

The retired builder spent four years battling the order through the planning inspectorate, High Court and Court of Appeal, but lost every challenge.



Mr Devine’s final appeal was dismissed in March 2023, but the house remained standing.

The council then prosecuted him for failing to comply with the enforcement notice.



Mr Devine was found guilty of one breach and appeared at Chester Crown Court for sentencing on November 6.

The offence is punishable by an unlimited fine.

However, Recorder Eric Lamb delayed sentencing after Mr Devine produced documents showing demolition work was scheduled.



The work is due to start today (November 14) and finish on November 28 to the tune of an estimated £20,000.

The judge also raised concerns that Mr Devine was unrepresented, having “spent all his money” appealing the case.

Sentencing was adjourned until December 21, with inspectors authorised to visit on December 14 to check the property has been knocked down.

Mr Devine said he was “not going to talk about” the case.

News.title: Jimmy Mizen’s killer given fresh  parole hearing despite being branded ‘known bully’ behind bars
News.content:
Next

JIMMY Mizen’s drill rapper killer has been given a fresh parole hearing just months after he was labelled a “known bully” behind bars.

Jake Fahri will go before the Parole Board in early 2027.



The thug, now 37, killed 16-year-old Jimmy at a bakery in Lee, South East London, in 2008.

He was jailed for life and served 14 years.



Fahri was released on licence in June 2023 but recalled in January 2025 for boasting about his crimes on drill rap songs.

He won a move to an open prison before Justice Secretary David Lammy blocked it.



But Jimmy’s mum Margaret Mizen, 74, told The Sun on Sunday last night: “When we hear there will be another parole hearing it brings all the emotions back, and it always comes around Christmas time.

“I just hope the Parole Board get it right this time, because last time they didn’t.

“They need to look at it seriously, and if they genuinely think he is ready to come out, we have to accept it.

“But they did say he was a bully last time, and if that hasn’t changed then it’s hard to see how he can come out.”



Millwall fan Jimmy was attacked by Fahri after the thug walked into the bakery and started an argument in May 2008.

The wannabe gangster, then 19, hurled a glass oven dish at Jimmy, severing an artery in his neck.

Fahri, who lived near the Mizens and already had convictions for burglary and assault, ran out of the shop and was described by a witness as “walking with a swagger”.

Fahri is entitled to one parole hearing at least every two years while on recall.

A Parole Board spokesman said: “Protecting the public is our priority.”

EMBASSY 'PAEDO' Senior US airman removed from Britain by Americans ‘sent video of himself committing sex act on bus’

A SENIOR US airman spirited out of Britain by the Americans sent a video of himself committing a sex act on a bus, a court martial heard.

Lt Col Michael Morris, 39, who was working at the US embassy in London, was allegedly in uniform in the footage.



He is also accused of swapping dozens of abuse images of children as young as two with his brother Benjamin, 33.

US spies flew Lt Col Morris to America without telling British police.



Claims aired in a military court at Joint Base Andrews near Washington DC make it clear he is accused of committing crimes on British soil.

A justice source said: “This makes it even more shocking the Americans acted without telling us.”

Benjamin, who was arrested in the US, is also charged with child abuse image offences.

The dawn raid in August, which The Sun on Sunday exclusively revealed, came after his brother Benjamin Morris was arrested in a sting, in June.

He denies the charges.

The charges relate to a period between March and April of this year.

News.title: Son of anti-Trump ex-CIA director arrested after ‘FBI uncovers sickening trove of child sex abuse images’
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TWISTED FIND Son of anti-Trump ex-CIA director arrested after ‘FBI uncovers sickening trove of child sex abuse images’







Next

THE son of ex-CIA Director John Brennan has been arrested for allegedly possessing a trove of child abuse material, reports say.

Kyle Brennan, 40, has been charged with transportation of child pornography, according to a federal complaint.



The case started when an account linked to Brennan was flagged to authorities by Adobe CyberTipline.

It reported the suspect for allegedly uploading illicit files of child abuse online.



The claims were submitted to the National Center for Missing and Exploited Children (NCMEC) in April and June, 2024.

The FBI’s Washington field office is involved in the probe.



On April 7, three files allegedly containing the illegal material were uploaded to the Adobe account.

A review of the files appeared to show a morphed image combining the face of a girl with the naked body of another child.

The girl was later identified as just 12 years old.

Comcast records also showed the IP address used to upload the files was registered to Brennan at an address in Virginia.



Apple also shared records confirming the private relay account was linked to the suspect.

In October, the FBI was alerted and a judge signed off on a warrant.

Investigators were then allowed to examine the files and seize Brennan’s phone.

On Friday, an analysis of his device, named “Kyle’s iphone (2)”, revealed 88 images of girls under the age of 18 engaging in sexual acts, prosecutors said.

A police complaint stated one image appeared to be a “fully nude, pubescent minor girl on a locker bench”.



It read: “The girl’s wrists and ankles were bound and her mouth was gagged.”

The Justice Department is also probing the suspect’s dad John Brennan, who once served under former President Barack Obama, over unrelated matters.

The investigation on Brennan Snr focuses on whether he lied to Congress in 2023 regarding the 2017 intelligence assessment on Russian election interference.

News.title: Two US tourists, 38 & 40, drown in holiday hotspot after being dragged under water by strong current on Caribbean trip
News.content:
TOURIST TRAGEDY Two US tourists, 38 & 40, drown in holiday hotspot after being dragged under water by strong current on Caribbean trip







Next

TWO American tourists have drowned in a holiday hotspot after being dragged under the water by strong currents during a Caribbean trip.

The tragic pair, a 38-year-old man and 40-year-old woman, were swimming with several others before they were pulled beneath the waves.

Police said the two victims were swimming near Bimini Island in an area where a sign had been placed warning of strong currents.

Some of the swimmers were rescued by a nearby ferry boat.





But the American swimmers were unresponsive when the vessel arrived to pick them out of the water.

Emergency services performed CPR on the pair when they arrived at hospital.

But they remained unresponsive and later died.

Local cops said: “Both victims were transported to the local clinic, where medical personnel continued life-saving efforts.



“Unfortunately, despite their efforts, both individuals were pronounced deceased by the attending physician shortly before 4pm.”

Police do not suspect foul play.

But an investigation has been launched to determine the full circumstances of the ordeal.

An autopsy will reveal their exact cause of death.



It comes after the heartbroken husband of a missing American tourist revealed she was allegedly seen alive more than four hours after she vanished on a dream vacation.

Elizabeth Waddell disappeared while going for a swim in the sea on the Caribbean island of Grenada on July 22.

News.title: PM hailed Milburn’s benefits recommendations – but it WON’T reduce Britain’s ballooning welfare bill
News.content:
Milburn’s Neet idea but costs still rising







Next

A GAGGLE of leftie Labour rebels are up in arms about Alan Milburn’s big welfare report.

The jobs czar is about to deliver his long-awaited inquiry into the causes of the shameful Neets crisis, which has seen a million young people locked out of jobs and education.



And, shock horror, Mr Milburn is actually proposing a reduction of some benefit cash for young people.

It is the first time a senior Labour figure has made genuine overtures towards reducing welfare since Keir Starmer tried to trim benefits by £5billion two years ago.



That proposal was shot down in flames by a rebellion of leftie backbench MPs faster than you could say “Universal Credit”.

It was the first nail in Starmer’s coffin.

But this time, his replacement Andy Burnham seems likely to accept Milburn’s recommendations and see off any minor rebellion.

The PM is hailing the report as a “watershed moment” for benefit provision.

He says: “It’s starting to point to a very different way of thinking about welfare.”

There is no doubt Mr Milburn will make many worthwhile and sensible proposals.



His aim to double the number of apprenticeships for young people is the type of policy The Sun on Sunday has long campaigned for.

But, despite the rebels, don’t imagine that these vital changes will reduce a welfare bill which is heading towards a staggering £430BILLION a year.

Mr Milburn proposes to cut benefits for some Neets which presently cost £4billion.

Even if he cuts half of them, that would only save £2billion.

The start-up costs of the report’s proposals are themselves estimated to be £6billion — and it may take a decade for them to be effective.



In the meantime, Britain’s benefits bill just keeps growing and growing.

Not so very different after all then, is it Prime Minister?

Got to be kidding

BRITS are used to being constantly chivvied along by the nanny state.

But this time the bureaucratic mollycoddling has gone too far.

A new Government guide warns students to take the bins out, clean the fridge and polish their phones.



Food Standards Agency officials have spent taxpayer cash advising freshers to wash their hands and stock up on cleaning products.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

But they should remember one thing:

If you treat people like toddlers, they will throw their toys out of the pram.

News.title: Husband cleared of driving his ex-wife to suicide arrested on suspicion of harassing her mum
News.content:
HUBBY 'BULLIED DEAD WIFE'S MA' Husband cleared of driving his ex-wife to suicide arrested on suspicion of harassing her mum







Next

A MAN cleared of driving his ex-wife to suicide has now been arrested on suspicion of harassing her mother, The Sun on Sunday can reveal.

Christopher Trybus, 44, was accused in court of a ‘Tsunami’ of sexual and violent abuse against former wife Tarryn Baird, who was allegedly left with injuries like a “car crash” victim.



Tarryn, 34, killed herself in the garage of the couple’s home in Swindon, Wilts, in November 2017.

Computer software company boss Mr Trybus was later charged with Tarryn’s manslaughter for allegedly driving her to kill herself in a landmark case which would have been the first conviction of its kind in English legal history.



However, Mr Trybus was found not guilty of manslaughter, two counts of rape and coercive control at Winchester Crown Court in April this year following a six-week trial.

Tarryn’s mother Michelle Baird was a key witness at the trial and told jurors about the sustained abuse her daughter allegedly suffered at the hands of Mr Trybus before her death.

Mrs Baird claims Mr Trybus has harassed her since the trial ended and she reported him to Wiltshire Police.

He was arrested last Friday (6 November) at his Swindon home on suspicion of harassment and released on bail pending further inquiries.

Mr Trybus strongly denies the allegation.

His lawyer Rishi Verma, partner at ABV Solicitors, said: “On behalf of Mr Trybus I confirm that he was arrested for an allegation of harassment.



“Mr Trybus denies the allegation. He will not provide any further comment at this stage as the investigation is ongoing.”

Wiltshire Police confirmed details of an arrest but declined to name Trybus under police protocols of not identifying suspects until they are charged.

A spokesperson for the force said: “A 44-year-old man was arrested in Swindon on Friday November 6th on suspicion of harassment.



“He has since been released on bail pending further enquiries.”

Mrs Baird, also of Swindon, became a key witness in her former son-in-law’s trial after discovering an audio recording on her late daughter’s phone.

The prosecution alleged the noise from the tape showed Mr Trybus raping Tarryn at the time, but the defence claimed it was rough sex.

She also told jurors that she saw bruises on her daughter’s body before her death.

Mrs Baird also recalled a conversation in which Mr Trybus allegedly told Tarryn that he would “snap her neck and dissolve her in acid”.



She also described how Mr Trybus exercised complete control over Tarryn, stating Tarryn had to “ask permission” to use her house and car keys, which were kept in the office where she worked for him after giving up her job in recruitment.

He was accused of monitoring Tarryn’s whereabouts, controlling her access to money, alienating her from her family and threatening to disclose private information about her.

Mrs Baird broke down in tears in the witness box, saying: “It is just so traumatising to relive this nightmare that I have lived for the last eight years.”

Tarryn had 177 contacts with Swindon Women’s Aid between during the 14 months leading up to her suicide and had also reported him to police.

Mr Trybus – who re-married in 2024 – denied the allegations against him and told jurors he was out of the country on the days of several allegations.



He also claimed his ex-wife had PTSD from witnessing carjackings in South Africa, where the couple met before moving to the UK and starting a romantic relationship.

His defence barrister said the entire case was built on an “agenda” of tackling violence against women and girls.

After he was acquitted, Trybus said his time under suspicion had “a profound impact on my life and on those closest to me”.

He said: “Right now, my focus is on moving forward and rebuilding my life with my family.”

RECOMMENDED STORIES

Mr Trybus also called for all victims of domestic violence to be “supported.”



An inquest into Tarryn’s death is still due to take place.

News.title: Man, 26, found dead after Coronation Street star issued plea in two-week search
News.content:
Man, 26, found dead after Coronation Street star issued plea in two-week search

Corrie and Benidorm star, Tony Maudsley, was among those who shared desperate pleas to find Dylan Mandaracas after he was last seen in October

View 2 Images Dylan Mandaracas (Image: BirminghamLive/BPM Media)

The body of a 26-year-old man has been found in a Birmingham canal after a Coronation Street star posted a missing person plea.

‌



‌



The man’s body was found in the Birmingham and Fazeley Canal, shortly before 9am today and West Midlands Police say they believe the body to be that of 26-year-old Dylan Mandaracas, who went missing last month.

‌



Dylan Mandaracas had last been seen on October 28 as he was walking by shops in Walmley Close, Birmingham Live reports.

‌



Desperate pleas to find him were shared after the young man's disappearance, including by Corrie and Benidorm star, Tony Maudsley. Maudsley shared an appeal on behalf of Dylan's dad, Christian Mandaracas, who is one of the star's old school friends.

The actor said at the time: "Posting this for a close friend whose son has gone missing. Hoping the power of social media can help this desperate family. Please share far & wide."

‌



View 2 Images CCTV of Dylan Mandaracas' last known movements (Image: Birmingham Police)

West Midlands Police said today that the body believed to be that of Dylan Mandaracas was discovered in the water just off Kingsbury Road. The force doesn't believe there are any suspicious circumstances surrounding the man's death.

‌



A spokesperson for the police said: "Shortly before 9am today (Saturday) we were called to reports that a man’s body had been discovered in a canal off the Kingsbury Road, Tyburn. Sadly, we believe the man to be 26-year-old Dylan Mandaracas, who had been reported missing on 2 November.

"We have carried out enquiries and don’t believe there are any suspicious circumstances surrounding his death. His family has been informed, and our thoughts are with them at this sad time.

Article continues below

"We will now be working to support the coroner."

News.title: At least six dead and 11 injured after bus overturns on motorway in southwestern Colombia
News.content:
At least six dead and 11 injured after bus overturns on motorway in southwestern Colombia

The Cootranscaquetá bus was travelling from San Vicente, Caqueta, to Bogota, Colombia's capital, and had 37 people on board

View 2 Images The coach was travelling from Florencia in Caquetá to Bogotá when it crashed in the Huila region (Image: Social Media)

At least six people have died and at least 15 have been seriously injured after a bus overturned on a motorway in Colombia.

‌



The incident occurred in the southwest of the South American country, with at least two minors reportedly among those killed. The Cootranscaquetá bus was carrying 37 passengers and was travelling to Bogota, the Colombian capital.

Preliminary investigations revealed that the driver of the bus may have briefly fallen asleep behind the wheel, causing the accident. According to El Tiempo, the driver is aged 26 and was seriously injured in the crash.

‌



View 2 Images The bus was heading to Bogota (Image: Social Media)

A police reports seen by the Associated Press states authorities were still trying to determine the exact circumstances under which the bus overturned in the department of Huila, but they believe the driver may have experienced an episode of "microsleep" - falling asleep for a few seconds.

‌



The bus departed on Friday evening from the community of San Vicente in Colombia’s southern department of Caqueta. The crash took place at around 2am on Saturday.

A statement from the Huila Traffic and Transportation Police said that the driver "lost control" of the bus, seemingly due to a "microsleep, resulting in the bus overturning onto its left side". Regarding the cause of the crash, Ariel Perdomo, manager of Cootranscaquetá, told El Tiempo: "It’s difficult to speculate, so we’re limiting ourselves to what the police tell us about this traffic accident."

Cablenoticias reports that among the fatalities are five adults and two minors.

News.title: Man in 'serious' condition after six men raid UK jewellers in terrifying daylight attack
News.content:
Man in 'serious' condition after six men raid UK jewellers in terrifying daylight attack

The man, aged 50, remains in hospital in life-threatening condition following the burglary at Lala Jewellers in Peterborough

View Image Lala Jewellers on Gladstone Street (Image: GoogleMaps)

A jewellery shop employee has suffered serious injuries following a violent burglary in Peterborough.

‌



‌



The incident took place as six men raided Lala Jewellers on Gladstone Street just before midday today. Two employees behind the counter were assaulted, Cambridgeshire Police said, and shelves were emptied.

‌



The suspects then fled in separate vehicles. Two of the six were wearing white traditional Pakistani clothing, police said.

‌



One of the two workers, a man aged 50, suffered serious injuries and was taken to hospital. He remains there in a life-threatening condition.

The other employee, a 30-year-old man, suffered minor injuries. Detective Inspector Tracy Sawyer said: "This is a very concerning incident which has left one man seriously injured and we are carrying out extensive enquiries to identify those responsible.

‌



"We would like to hear from anyone who was in the Gladstone Street area at around the time of the robbery and saw anything suspicious either before or after the incident.

"We would also urge anyone with CCTV, doorbell or dashcam footage from the area which may have captured something relevant to please get in touch."

Article continues below

Anyone with information is asked to contact the police quoting reference 35/88602/26.

News.title: Russell Brand's wife Laura Gallacher faces difficult decision as sex fiend is 'moved into main wing'
News.content:
Russell Brand's young family faces a difficult decision over whether to relocate back to the UK or remain in America as he begins his 10-and-a-half year sentence for rape and sexual assault.

Prior to the trial, Brand had been living in Florida with his family. The disgraced former comedian, 51, even threw a beach party before the family flew back to Britain for the court case in October, with those close to him reportedly confident he would walk free.

But following his lengthy sentence, he was moved to a main wing at HMP Wandsworth in southwest London, and may be transferred to another jail known informally as Monster Mansion. His wife Laura must now decide whether to support him in England.

A prison insider said: "Wakefield is quite literally known as Monster Mansion - it is the place where Britain's most vile monsters are holed up.

"We are talking brutal crimes - murder, rape, sex assaults. Some against children. Three quarters of the inmates in Wakefield are in for sexually assaulting people. It houses the worst of the worst, and probably is not a place where you'd want to take children to be honest."

Ian McNabb won't be inducted into music Hall of Fame after Russell Brand comments READ MORE :

Joanne McNally brands Katherine Ryan a 'hero' for warning about Russell Brand READ MORE :

3 View 3 Images Laura Gallacher pictured with her broadcaster sister, Kirsty (Image: Getty Images Europe) 3 View 3 Images Brand was convicted of raping a fan and sexually assaulting three other women (Image: INSTAGRAM)

They added: "It is the same for all prisoners with kids at home of course, it is an individual decision on whether you want your children in that environment. But if they want regular face to face access to their dad, it may mean that they have to relocate."

Convicted rapist Brand had uprooted his wife and their three young children from Oxfordshire, England, to Santa Rosa Beach, Florida, in late 2024, while retaining their English home, reports the Daily Star. It has been suggested that Laura and her three children are now weighing up a permanent return to their property in Henley-on-Thames, Oxfordshire, and enrolling the children into the British way of life.

The source added: "Children are allowed in Wakefield, they obviously have to be with an adult, and they still have to be listed as an approved contact before being allowed in.

"Laura will have to provide ID like a birth certificate or passport of the children to make them official visitors, and they will all have to be searched if they choose to have a face to face visit, so it is not an overly nice experience.

"They will all be patted down and could even be sniffed by drug detection dogs. It is a lot. But it is necessary and part of this new world they are now having to navigate."

News.title: 'Predators thrive when complaints are dismissed and too many stay silent'
News.content:
'Predators thrive when complaints are dismissed and too many stay silent'

EXCLUSIVE: TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak warns 'even in 2026 too many workplaces still have cultures and systems that allow abuse to flourish and fail women when they report it'

View 2 Images Russell Brand was sentenced to more than 10 years in prison after being convicted of rape and sexual assaults (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

This week has been a grim reminder of the scale of violence against women and girls in our society.

On Monday Russell Brand was sentenced to more than ten years in prison for rape and sexual assault. Now there have been allegations that David Walliams, who denies wrongdoing, used his fame and power to prey on teenage girls and young women for sex.

These are two different cases but our thoughts are with those who came forward and with all survivors who have experienced sexual violence, including those who may never feel able to speak publicly about what happened to them.

The headlines have shone a spotlight on individual men. But they should also force us to ask a wider question. What was known? What was suspected? And why were the warning signs ignored for so long?

Even people who say they knew nothing of Brand's crimes have described his behaviour towards women as an “open secret”. In 2004 Jonathan Ross joked about Walliams “going home with a 15-year-old” in front of a packed audience at the British Comedy Awards.

Those details matter because sexual predators rarely operate in complete secrecy. Too often there are rumours, concerns, warning signs and witnesses. Too often people look the other way.

This should be a moment for women - for every woman reading these stories and recognising something of her own experiences in the headlines.

Nigel Farage was guest on Russell Brand’s US podcast months after sexual assault claims made public READ MORE :

Nandy demands answers from TV bosses over action they're taking to protect women from celebrity abusers READ MORE :

View 2 Images TUC General Secretary Paul Nowak said it must be a moment for men to step up (Image: Tim Merry/Staff Photographer)

But it cannot be a fight for women alone. This is a moment for men to step up too. It is a moment to think honestly about the times we have laughed off sexist “banter”, witnessed inappropriate behaviour and said nothing, or chosen comfort over challenge when faced with misogyny.

As General Secretary of the TUC, I know the trade union movement has its own responsibility to confront these issues. We have a duty to tackle sexism where it exists and to help make workplaces safer for everyone. Because workplace culture is at the heart of many of these stories.

The uncomfortable truth is that even in 2026 too many workplaces still have cultures and systems that allow abuse to flourish and fail women when they report it. Half of women say they have experienced sexual harassment at work. The risks are even higher for Black women, disabled women, younger women and LGBT+ women.

In most cases the perpetrator is a male colleague. Nearly one in five women say the harassment came from their direct manager or another person with power over them.

That is why new workplace protections introduced by the government last month are so important. For the first time employers have a legal duty to take all reasonable steps to prevent sexual harassment, including harassment by customers, clients and other third parties. This is a significant shift.

The burden should never have been on women to protect themselves. The responsibility belongs to employers to create workplaces where harassment is prevented, challenged and dealt with.

But passing a law is only the start. The government has promised to set out clearly what employers must do to meet their new responsibilities. Ministers now need to get on with it so every employer understands exactly what is expected of them.

There are not just a “few bad apples”. Sexual predators exist in television studios, offices, warehouses, hospitals, shops, and yes, in the trade union movement too. They thrive in cultures where complaints are dismissed, rumours are ignored and too many people stay silent.

Changing that culture is the challenge before us. And if this week's events teach us anything it is that silence protects perpetrators. Speaking up protects women. Now is the time to make sure we never confuse the two again.

Rape Crisis England & Wales is the feminist charity working to end child sexual abuse, rape, sexual assault, sexual harassment and all other forms of sexual violence. Call the free 24/7 Support Line on 0808 500 2222 or chat online at 247sexualabusesupport.org.uk.

News.title: Boy in hospital after hit-and-run while crossing UK road
News.content:
Boy in hospital after hit-and-run while crossing UK road

Emergency services were called to the Newry Road area of Armagh on Saturday afternoon after a young boy was hit by a car. Police are urging the driver of the VW Golf to come forward

View Image A child has been injured in a hit-and-run (Image: Google)

A young boy is receiving hospital treatment after being struck in a hit-and-run collision in Armagh on Saturday afternoon, police have confirmed.

‌



‌



Emergency services were called to the Newry Road area of the town following reports that the child had been hit by a vehicle.

‌



Officers have issued an appeal urging the driver involved in the incident to come forward.

‌



Sergeant Bigger said: “We received a report at around 2.30pm that a boy child had been hit by a silver VW Golf while crossing the road.

“Unfortunately, the driver failed to remain at the scene, so we’re keen to speak to anyone who witnessed the collision to get in touch with us, including the driver of the Golf.

‌



“Our officers attended the scene, along with colleagues from the Northern Ireland Ambulance Service, and the boy was taken on to hospital for treatment to injuries that are not believed to be life-threatening.

“Our inquiries are ongoing and we would appeal to anyone with any information which might assist – including dash-cam, CCTV or other footage – to contact police using our witness appeal form at reporting.psni.police.uk/appeals.”

Article continues below

Alternatively, people can call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111 or online at http://crimestoppers-uk.org/

News.title: Inside the £14million cocaine plot linking Britain’s streets to the world’s most wanted drug kingpin
News.content:
Inside the £14million cocaine plot linking Britain’s streets to the world’s most wanted drug kingpin

EXCLUSIVE: Around £14m of cocaine linked to Dutch crime lord "Chubby Jos" was seized before completing its planned 5,000 mile journey to the address in the Bordesley Green area of Birmingham

View 7 Images Dutch cocaine kingpin Jos Leijdekkers, known as 'Chubby Jos' (Image: Daily Record)

From Bogota to Birmingham via West Africa, this is the extra-ordinary journey of cocaine bound for British users.

We can reveal the world’s most wanted coke trafficker – Dutch drugs kingpin Jos Leijdekkers, known as “Chubby Jos” – has been linked to a huge shipment said to have been bound for a suburban semi in Birmingham.

Around £14million of the class-A powder was seized in Liberia before completing its planned 5,000-mile journey from Colombia to the address in the Bordesley Green area of the city.

Officials in Liberia discovered the consignment disguised as stock cubes on a Brussels Airways flight heading to Heathrow in June. British national Usman Ali has been charged in the West African country, along with four others, in connection with the plot and is currently the subject of an international manhunt.

We have seen the indictment in which Ali is named, along with the Birmingham address linked to him where the drugs were said to be destined.

View 7 Images Liberian Senator Amara Konneh (Image: Philip Coburn)

The shipment had come from neighbouring Sierra Leone and has been linked by police to Dutch cocaine kingpin Leijdekkers.

A second £230million cocaine seizure, the largest in Liberia’s history, was stopped in the capital Monrovia in July. Former Vice President Jewel Howard-Taylor was charged with drug trafficking, money laundering and other offences in connection with this shipment.

Croatian national Nikola Ivancic is accused of masterminding the plot. Leijdekkers, 35, has built one of the world’s most powerful cocaine empires from his base in West Africa, under the alleged protection of some of Sierra Leone’s most powerful figures.

Liberian Senator Amara Konneh visited Britain this week to lobby MPs and peers in an effort to win support for his fight against Leijdekkers’ organised crime group.

View 7 Images The house in Birmingham where the drugs were allegedly due to be delivered (Image: google)

Mr Konneh told us: “The UK and Liberia need to come together now to deal with this common threat. We see a network that is trying to infiltrate our institutions, that is trying to corrupt our systems to find safe havens in our county. It is the same network that is supplying the streets of London and Birmingham.

“We see a creeping threat with this drug trafficking. If we don’t see powers like Britain talking about this, and using its convening power in institutions like the UN Security Council to support Liberia, we will have a bigger problem in the future.” Mr Konneh said Ali could be hiding in Britain and appealed to UK law enforcement to track him down.

View 7 Images This map illustrates the journey the drugs are said to have taken

He said: “We were hoping that the British authorities will accelerate their search for him here in England and hopefully make him available to Liberia to face justice. If not they could work with our authorities to review the evidence against him and hopefully prosecute him here in England.”

Liberian President Joseph Boakai has made a request to the British government for assistance. Mr Konneh added: “I know that conversation is happening. What I want to see is a more robust partnership, not just in one case, but between our institutions so we can share intelligence.

‌



“I’m not here to ask for aid. I am just saying that we face an existential threat from this network which is targeting our young people and our security people who are working in very difficult circumstances.”

View 7 Images The seized cocaine being burned in Liberia (Image: AFP via Getty Images)

‌



A specialist unit at the National Crime Agency is reportedly investigating Leijdekkers’ links to the UK. His drug operation, said to be worth more than Sierra Leone’s entire national budget, reflects a shift in the cocaine trade. West Africa now accounts for at least 30% of the drug reaching Europe, according to the Global Initiative Against Transnational Organised Crime.

In an attempt to persuade one of Leijdekkers’ contacts to betray him, Dutch prosecutors this month announced a £1.6million reward for information leading to his arrest.

‌



He has lived a brazen exile in Sierra Leone, a former British colony, since at least 2022. He was filmed at a New Year’s Day church service alongside the country’s first family, and handing out gifts at a party to senior officials, including the head of the drug police. He is believed to be in a relationship with a daughter of Sierra Leone’s President Julius Maada Bio, and they reportedly have a child.

Mr Konneh believes that the UK has not done enough to raise concerns about Leijdekkers’ influence in the region. He said: “I think we need to see the British government do more, not just in Sierra Leone but in the other countries along the West African coast that this individual is allegedly trying to use to expand his network in our region.”

‌



View 7 Images Leijdekkers filmed at church service (Image: EUROPOL/AFP via Getty Images)

Since the arrest of Irish crime boss Daniel Kinahan in Dubai in August, Leijdekkers is believed to be the world’s most-wanted drug smuggler.

‌



He uses the pseudonym Omar Sheriff, but is known as “Bolle Jos”, Dutch for chubby. The kingpin is wanted by the Dutch and Belgian authorities, who have sentenced him to more than 100 years in his absence. At least 14 people have reportedly been murdered in Sierra Leone on Leijdekkers’ orders, including high- ranking police officers.

Prosecutors cited the case of a young Amsterdam woman, Naima Jillal, who vanished in 2019 after encrypted messages linked Leijdekkers to her disappearance.

‌



Dutch special forces are believed to have come close to capturing the villain twice this year as he travelled between Sierra Leone and Liberia by boat, but the operations were aborted.

View 7 Images Naima Jillal vanished in 2019 (Image: Daily Record)

‌



The European Commission suspended £15million in aid to Sierra Leone last month, which the Dutch authorities said was punishment for the refusal to extradite Leijdekkers. Mr Konneh fears he is attempting to expand his empire into Liberia after the June seizure was linked to him.

The senator sees the trade as the biggest threat to his country since an estimated 200,000 people were killed during civil wars that ravaged Liberia between 1989 and 2003.

‌



Former president Charles Taylor is serving a 50-year sentence in the UK for war crimes, including the use of child soldiers. Figures published last week revealed deaths from cocaine in England and Wales have nearly quadrupled in a decade, overtaking those attributed to heroin for the first time.

In England alone, the Home Office estimates the market is worth £9.8bn.

‌



Mr Konneh said: “The demand for cocaine here in Britain is fuelling a potentially destabilising force in my country that is still recovering from a civil war. We have managed to restore stability. We have had four successive democratic transitions. Our people are moving on and then all of a sudden we see this menace that is trying to destroy all of that.

“Just like we saw the warlords use child soldiers, we can potentially see the drug lords using child traffickers if we do not intervene now.”

The Home Office said: “The National Crime Agency and Border Force are working closely with partners across West Africa to disrupt drug trafficking routes and dismantle the criminal gangs behind them.”

News.title: Man, 21, stabbed to death by Tottenham park pictured and murder probe launched
News.content:
Man, 21, stabbed to death by Tottenham park pictured and murder probe launched

Emergency services were called to reports of the attack on Lordship Lane in Tottenham, north London, with a police cordon still in place today

View 2 Images A tent and police cordon on Lordship Lane this morning (Image: Twitter/X/@ediz1975)

A murder investigation has been launched after a 21-year-old man was stabbed to death outside a park in London.

‌



Emergency services were called to reports of the attack on Lordship Lane, near Lordship Recreation Ground, in Tottenham, north London, at around 6pm yesterday. The victim was treated by paramedics at the scene but died from his injuries.

The victim has been named by the Metropolitan Police as Thomas Oduro from Tottenham and his family are being supported by officers. No arrests have yet been made, as detectives continue to carry out enquiries.

MyLondon reports a team of forensic officers were spotted at the scene overnight, with a large cordon still in place near the park's entrance earlier today. A police tent was also seen on the road, just metres from the park gates.

View 2 Images Thomas Oduro

Officers have now urged anyone holding any information about the incident to contact them. Detective Chief Inspector Phil Clarke said this afternoon: "Thomas’s family have suffered a devastating loss. Our thoughts are with them, and they continue to be supported by specialist officers.

"Enquiries continue at the scene and there will be an increased police presence in the area over the coming days. As part of our investigation, I’m urging anyone who was in the area of Lordship Recreation Ground around 18:00hrs on Friday, or who has information which may be relevant, to speak to officers or get in touch as soon as possible."

Anyone with information is urged to contact police via 101, quoting CAD 5439/13NOV26. Alternatively, call Crimestoppers anonymously on 0800 555 111.

News.title: Neets review won't be for the faint-hearted - and will test Burnham's appetite for a welfare fight
News.content:
It's an ugly acronym. And it's an even uglier situation.

The reality of so-called "Neets" in the UK - young people who haven't got jobs, aren't studying or being trained up - has seen hundreds upon hundreds of thousands in their late teens or early-20s struggle to find a decent future for well over a decade.

It costs the taxpayer billions. And the human cost is variously described as a disaster, a national shame, even a moral crisis.

When the phrase Neet was first coined by Tony Blair's Downing Street in 1999, the focus was on 170,000 or so teenagers who were not in education, employment or training. After many attempts at solving the problem, add in a pandemic and years of a sluggish economy, it's acute - with nearly a million under-25s in that situation.

A tome full of proposals to try and fix it once and for all will be published on Tuesday, after a year in the making.

How the government reacts will test its appetite and capacity for radical change, and the prime minister's real, not rhetorical, hunger for tricky political arguments.

The canny smooth talker behind the huge review, former Labour MP Alan Milburn, wants you to know that Andy Burnham knows exactly what's coming.

Speaking to me in Liverpool, where in Merseyside 14.5% of 16 to 24-year-olds are unemployed,, external he tells me: "All the way through, the prime minister, the chancellor, all the ministers, they know what's going on. It won't be a surprise to them when this is launched and that gives it a fighting chance of actually being implemented."

But his collection of proposals is not for the faint-hearted.

On top of a plan to stop under-25s claiming the main sickness and disability benefits, Milburn will argue for a dramatic shift in the balance of what the taxpayer spends on benefits for young people compared with what is spent on support to help them get into work.

He says the amount spent on young people's benefits is 25 times as much as that on employment support - and he wants to shift it to a drastically different two to one.

He won't put specific numbers on it yet, but accepts openly that means a significant number of young people losing their benefits or facing cuts.

But that would come with a chunky expansion of the amount of further education, training, health support and likely jobs subsidised by the taxpayer too. A big cut to state support on one side of the ledger, but a big increase on the other.

And to make sure that government gets really serious about improving the mess, Milburn is asking for a new law that would give young people a guarantee of help and support - a job, an apprenticeship, a training place, or perhaps health treatment so they are able to work - an "opportunity guarantee".

He told me he won't fall into the "elephant's trap", where a feisty teenager could sue the prime minister if they didn't get the job they fancied. But the idea is to put a legal duty on the authorities in a similar vein to councils' obligation to look after children in care, or to provide accommodation or advice to homeless people.

News.title: Alleged Russell Brand rape victim wants age of consent law changed
News.content:
Warning - this story contains graphic content

A woman who has alleged that she was raped by Russell Brand when she was 16 has waived her right to anonymity and is campaigning for a staggered age of consent in an interview with the Sunday Times.

Mia Latter was one of six women who made allegations against Brand in 2023 as part of a Times, Sunday Times and Channel 4's Dispatches investigation. She was known under the pseudonym 'Alice'. Brand denied the allegations at the time.

None of the women in the 2023 media investigation were complainants in Brand's recent criminal trial.

On Monday the entertainer was sentenced to 10 and a half years for one count of rape and three counts of sexual assault. He was acquitted of two counts of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.

The Sunday Times reported that Latter had initially described the allegation about Brand to them as a sexual assault and that is how they reported it in their 2023 investigation.

Latter, 37, "now calls this allegation rape", the paper said.

Latter said she was 16 when she met Brand, who was 30 at the time, when she was on her way home from a shopping trip. She said Brand was working at MTV.

She told the paper: "I think people were so struck by my story because of the age difference and the clear imbalance [in power],"

She said Brand told her to keep their relationship secret from her school friends and claimed that he referred to her as "the child" in front of his entourage.

It was towards the end of their relationship that Latter was allegedly orally raped by Brand, according to the Sunday Times.

Latter said that she was now campaigning for the introduction of a "staggered" age of consent that would prohibit relationships between 16- and 17-year-olds and adults.

"I don't want to criminalise teenagers having sex with each other," she told the paper. "If you're between the ages of 16 and 18, it seems reasonable that you can have relationships with each other, and [teenagers] are always going to. But â¦ if you're in your thirties, forties and fifties and you're trying to have a relationship with someone under the age of 18, it [should be] a criminal offence."

She also told the paper that she would not continue with the criminal process so she could focus on her campaign.

In her interview with the Sunday Times she said that the CPS decided not to include her as part of Brand's criminal trial but the police wanted her to be part of a "subsequent trial".

A Met Police spokesperson said: "Officers launched an investigation in January 2026 after receiving an allegation of rape.

"Detectives sought advice from the Crown Prosecution Service to determine how best to proceed, and officers were advised that further information was needed before a charging decision could be made.

"This investigation remains ongoing. We understand the delay has been distressing for this victim-survivor. However, our focus has been on putting forward the best possible evidence."

A spokesperson for the Crown Prosecution Service said it would "continue to work closely with investigators to provide advice and make sure cases progress as quickly as possible".

News.title: New Orleans port files $1m lawsuit over 'miracle on the Mississippi' tanker collision
News.content:
The paddlewheel cruise ship, American Heritage, was left on its side and partially submerged in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt on Friday afternoon.

The court documents added that the port terminal "was significantly damaged" in the incident.

The tanker, the M/V Atlantic Asphalt, its owner Nave Shipping SA, and its management company, Thome Ship Management Pte Ltd, are all named in the federal court lawsuit filed on Friday in the Eastern District of Louisiana court.

Officials are still investigating the full extent of the damage from the crash, as well as the cause, but the lawsuit says the port is looking for money to cover cleanup, inspections, repairs and other expenses.

The lawsuit requests that the tanker be seized and sold to pay for the damage. It also alleges that the collision "occurred as a result of the negligence, gross negligence, fault or carelessness" of the ship and operating companies.

It alleges that the tanker and companies failed "to use all available means to avoid the risk" of colliding with the riverboat.

Nave Shipping is a subsidiary of the China State Shipbuilding Corporation. BBC has contacted the China State Shipbuilding Corporation for comment.

Thome Ship Management has also been contacted. The firm said in a statement on Saturday that the crew of the Atlantic Asphalt were safe and accounted for.

"OSM Thome is fully complying with the local authorities as they carry out the necessary investigations," it said.

There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority.

Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort.

The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway.

News.title: Wales stun New Zealand to end 73-year losing streak
News.content:
Nations Championship

Wales (21) 35

Tries: T Williams, Lake, Griffin, James, Rees-Zammit Cons: Costelow 5

New Zealand (21) 28

Tries: Ratima, Sititi, Fineanganofo, Lakai Cons: Mo'unga 4.

Wales celebrated a first victory against New Zealand in 73 years with a brilliant performance to spark astonishing scenes in Cardiff.

Steve Tandy's unfancied side lifted a nation as they broke a 34-match losing sequence against the All Blacks that stretched back to 1953.

In a nine-try Nations Championship thriller at the Principality Stadium, Wales led 14-0, 21-7 and 35-21 before they held off New Zealand with a wonderful defensive display in the final quarter, led by flankers James Botham and Jac Morgan and lock Dafydd Jenkins.

The home side produced a stunning start with tries from inspirational scrum-half Tomos Williams and captain Dewi Lake inside the first six minutes.

Prop Archie Griffin also added a first-half try, but New Zealand responded with scores from scrum-half Cortez Ratima, number eight Wallace Sititi and wing Fehi Fineanganofo to level the score 21-21 at half-time.

Wales centre Eddie James and wing Louis Rees-Zammit scored early second-half tries before New Zealand flanker Peter Lakai pulled one back.

The remarkable Wales defence followed as they held up the All Blacks three times over the line to stop New Zealand scoring, to evoke wild celebrations.

News.title: Beauty advent calendars can cost hundreds - but are they value for money?
News.content:
It's easy to see the appeal of a beauty advent calendar. Like many women at this time of year, Julia says she often finds herself tempted to splurge on one - especially a perfume calendar. But she takes quite an unsentimental approach.

"I always look at what's in them. If I like enough of the fragrances, I'll buy it," says the 39-year old, who works as a senior commercial manager in engineering.

Luxury advent calendars are supposed to offer the thrill of a surprise but, for Julia, it is more important she actually wants the items inside - a thought that is also striking more and more customers in the wake of the scandal over the Skims calendar.

News.title: How to shake hands and make eye contact - the lessons preparing pupils for the world of work
News.content:
There is a sudden buzz of conversation in a Year 10 class as teenagers split into pairs, sit down opposite each other and start conducting mock job interviews.

It is not for a forthcoming exam. These 14- and 15-year-olds at Sandbach High School and Sixth Form College are working on skills that should help them when they leave school and try to enter the workforce.

Today, they are learning the art of a successful job interview. Around the room, pupils are practising firm handshakes and making good eye contact.

They are rehearsing how to answer questions that you might expect to be asked in a job interview, such as "When was the last time you worked in a team?" and "Tell me about a time you made a mistake at work".

None of them has even reached working age yet, but in forthcoming lessons they'll also be learning about how to write a CV and what their rights at work are. It is all part of dedicated career lessons that they get every fortnight alongside their usual classes.

There are nearly a million young people across the UK - one in eight of all those aged 16 to 24 - who are not in education, employment or training - or Neet - according to the latest estimates.

Prime Minister Andy Burnham has called the high number both a "moral failure" and an "economic catastrophe".

News.title: Holly Humberstone: People can't connect to a pop star who's 'too polished'
News.content:
You might know her as a pop star, endorsed by everyone from Taylor Swift to Sam Fender, but Holly Humberstone has a secret double life.

In her spare time, the singer-songwriter is literally a cat burglar.

"We've stolen one of our neighbours' cats by accident," she laughs, in a Zoom call from her fixer-upper in New Cross, south-east London.

"He's a tiny little black cat who's come into our garden and simply chosen us."

Under the slightest scrutiny, however, her story crumbles like a biscuit in a hot cup of tea.

"OK, we've been coercing him into the house with treats," she admits. "He's just so cute.

"But we're not trying to keep him. We literally push him out every night."

Humberstone's excuse for this feline felony is that, last year, her parents sold her childhood home in Lincolnshire, external and moved to Wales â taking her pets with them.

One, a cat called Tsuki, had even been immortalised in the song Lucy as a confidante who listens to her problems but "never judges".

"Oh, she knows some secrets!" laughs the singer. "I'm so glad she can't talk."

"We actually tried to bring her to London with us, but she's a countryside cat and she hated it so much. We had to send her to Wales where she can be free and frolic."

Her parents' relocation was disruptive for the human Humberstones, too.

Their house, a "freezing cold, falling down" property 20 minutes outside of Grantham, played a huge part in the singer's success.

Her early EPs were all written there, inspiring the "wonky sonics" of her indie-leaning pop sound. The 2021 single Haunted House is even dedicated to the "friendly" spirits who inhabited the property.

"It's a place I always felt I could go back to, to remind myself of who I am," she says.

Instead, she spent 2025 "packing up 23 years of stuff my family and I had accumulated", from her old ballet shoes and poetry books to forgotten bits of jewellery.

News.title: Judo champion shakes up French  presidential race with surprise candidacy
News.content:
Apart from an overwhelming urge to pin one's opponent to the floor of the house, there is no obvious connection between politics and the world of top-level judo.

That has not stopped France's much-garlanded world heavyweight champion Teddy Riner from throwing his hat into the ring for next April's presidential race.

The Guadeloupe-born 37-year-old may have no experience of public office, no party behind him, and as yet no manifesto. All so far is a slogan La France qu'on aime (The France we love), a declaration on social media, and a campaign visit to a hospital in the Seine-Saint-Denis suburb of northern Paris.

But it would be a foolhardy pundit who would totally write off his chances.

Riner is, after all, one of the most popular figures in modern-day France, regularly topping the polls for embodying the nation's "values". He is a proven winner, with five Olympic golds and 11 world championships under his belt, as well as a successful career in business.

More than 28 million people have watched his election broadcast on Instagram and X, shot with proper presidential decorum against a backdrop of books and a French flag. Some 22% told an Ifop poll within 24 hours they "could" vote for him.

News.title: Young people should have legal guarantee of job or training, Milburn tells BBC
News.content:
Prime Minister Andy Burnham has described Milburn's forthcoming report as a "watershed moment," but stopped short of committing to implementing its recommendations in full.

Burnham also insisted paying for the reforms would not mean "more money" but "spending differently" in government when pressed on the large upfront investment they are expected to require.

Asked whether he would accept the politically sensitive report in full, Burnham declined to provide that "blanket assurance".

Speaking at the Welsh Labour conference on Saturday, Burnham said that the report addressed the "youth detachment" that has been on the rise since the pandemic.

"It can't be right that we've stripped away support from young people as a society, as life is getting harder for them and growing up is getting more difficult," he said.

The prime minister added that the government was also looking at a new vision for schooling that is "not focused solely on the university route" and which offers technical education alongside traditional academic learning.

Lord Blunkett, a former Labour home secretary, told the BBC that money from cutting benefits spending should be reassigned to supporting employment "at least in the immediate future".

Speaking on Radio 4's Today programme, he said reforms should focus on "transferring resource that currently goes into paying for failure, keeping youngsters at home, isolated, lonely, into actually putting the money in and the resource and the commitment in to making those jobs available".

Conservative Party leader Kemi Badenoch has previously said the government should not be spending "lots of time" on employment schemes, which she said would ultimately fail.

Her party and Reform UK have argued for significant cuts to welfare, including to fund a boost to defence.

Reform economy spokesman Robert Jenrick said: "This review is pointless unless we get action from Burnham straight away.

"It cannot be right that this continues for another 10 years before the youth benefits bill comes down."

Green Party leader Zack Polanski said it was "disappointing" the Milburn review had "come up with the same tired conclusions" on youth unemployment.

Polanski added: "Using benefit sanctions to force young people into low-paid, insecure work doesn't solve the structural inequalities they face, and it deepens poverty."

The Liberal Democrats want the government to introduce a 100-hour work experience guarantee and a careers coach for every young person.

They believe this would equip youngsters with the best possible skills before they leave school.

The TUC - the umbrella group for unions in the UK - welcomed Milburn's proposal of a legal guarantee as a "game changer", describing the country's number of Neets as a "national emergency".

But it stressed that funding for additional support for young people should not come from public service budgets. "In further education, funding needs to be targeted at the workforce, as well as provision, to tackle the recruitment and retention crisis and massive pay disparities in the sector," it said.

"A zero sum approach would be wrong and counter-productive."

News.title: Man dies after being stabbed by gang of masked men
News.content:
A murder investigation has been launched after a 27-year-old man was stabbed in Manchester.

Officers were called to Moss Bank in the Crumpsall area of the city shortly after 01:30 GMT following reports that a man had suffered several stab wounds. He later died from his injuries in an ambulance.

Greater Manchester Police (GMP) said initial inquiries suggested the victim had been attacked by "a number of males" all believed to have been wearing dark clothing and balaclavas.

The suspects are believed to have fled the scene in the direction of Ash Tree Road, said a force spokesperson who added that no arrests had been made and inquiries were continuing.

News.title: UK ethics watchdog chief steps back from role over sexual misconduct claims
News.content:
The head of the government's main ethics watchdog has stepped back after it emerged he was investigated in a previous job over alleged sexual misconduct involving female colleagues, and had, in one case, been sanctioned.

Stuart Sterling was appointed as the first chief executive of the newly formed Ethics and Integrity Commission in October 2025.

The existence of the allegations against Sterling, and the investigations into them, were first reported by the Sunday Times.

Following the report, a government spokesperson said: "These are serious allegations. Stuart Sterling has stepped back from his role while we swiftly establish the facts."

The Labour Party promised in its 2024 manifesto to create the commission to "ensure probity in government" in response to scandals during the Covid pandemic.

As its head, Sterling's role included advising the prime minister on tackling misconduct in public life.

The Sunday Times reported that, in 2003, Sterling had been subject to a "full misconduct hearing" when he was a junior officer with Northamptonshire Police in what was treated as a case "of sexual harassment".

The paper said he had been accused of inappropriately touching the breasts of a female colleague in a police station, and a male colleague who allegedly witnessed the event had reported him to his superiors. It reported that he had been suspended on full pay.

A representative for Mr Sterling said: "Stuart states that a full disciplinary process was held regarding the complaint in 2002. He complied with this fully. It resulted in a sanction."

The Sunday Times reported that he was given a financial penalty of two weeks' pay. It said that, at the time, that was the maximum sanction possible short of forced resignation. He then received two police commendations and was promoted to be a detective sergeant.

The Sunday Times said that by 2008 Mr Sterling had been reported to the force again after another allegation of sexual misconduct against a female colleague, this time at a social gathering outside work.

Mr Sterling's representative said: "He denies that the alleged incident in 2008 ever took place. He was never subject to any criminal investigation, but the allegation was examined by professional standards".

The representative added: "He was not required to resign from the force. He left voluntarily".

Northamptonshire Police has confirmed that it holds a digital record of a misconduct process from 2002.

It did not comment on the later allegation.

In 2009, Sterling joined the Cabinet Office. It is not clear what vetting process he underwent. He has since served in a variety of senior roles and in 2019 was seconded to the National Police Chiefs' Council. In 2023 he received an OBE for helping to plan the funeral of Queen Elizabeth.

It is understood the Cabinet Office will now examine whether appropriate and correct disclosures of information were made.

News.title: King jokes with Elton John as he marks 78th birthday with radio show
News.content:
King Charles and Sir Elton John joked about the problems of ageing as the pair joined for a special radio show to coincide with the monarch's 78th birthday.

Sir Elton, 79, was joined on his regular Rocket Hour radio show for a special episode during which the King shared his musical memories as the pair chose 14 songs together.

The programme also marked the 50th anniversary of the King's Trust and highlighted how musicians have supported the charity's efforts.

"We and the Trust are definitely still standing," the King said, as he highlighted Sir Elton's track I'm Still Standing as one of his favourites because of the song's "message of resilience".

The music legend joked in reply: "I'm still sitting now, though" giving a large laugh, with the King chuckling: "With occasional bits dropping off here and there. I know this is a terrible problem as we get older."

The special was recorded last month at Apple Music Studios in south London and premiered on Saturday morning.

The King recalled Sir Elton's 1986 performance at Wembley Arena, which marked the charity's 10th anniversary.

"I suspect that no-one who was present on that night in 1986 could possibly forget your performance of I'm Still Standing," King Charles said.

"I know people in all kinds of circumstances find this song inspiring, not only for its marvellous spirit, but also its message of resilience. And certainly, 40 years on from that remarkable concert, we and the Trust are definitely still standing."

News.title: Burnham suggests Welsh Labour lost sight of devolution as review criticises ex-first minister's strategy
News.content:
The prime minister has told members of his party that Welsh Labour may have lost sight of some of the principles of devolution before it was thrown out of power in a historic election defeat.

On Saturday morning Andy Burnham addressed the first Welsh Labour conference since May's Senedd election.

He suggested the previous Labour government did not do enough to pass powers down to communities, and said it was "hard" to accept the party was no longer in power after 27 years of running the Welsh government.

He spoke before a review into what went wrong concluded that former First Minister Eluned Morgan's political strategy of calling out Westminster played a role in the party losing power.

The report by Prof Anand Menon, of PF Global, said Morgan's calls for constitutional change like the devolution of policing and the Crown Estate did not get through to voters.

A source close to the former first minister said it was "ludicrous" to suggest that Morgan was focused on constitutional issues.

Meanwhile, Welsh Labour leader Ken Skates has criticised his party for focusing too much on powers for the Senedd.

In a subdued speech, Burnham said he wanted to see "one Labour team" where "everyone" was "signed up and on the same page."

He spoke ahead of the publication of a review of what went wrong at the election.

Since he became prime minister he has been lobbying the Welsh government to devolve more powers to local councils.

"Somewhere along the way perhaps we lost sight of some of the principles that drove devolution in the first place.

"We probably stopped listening as much as we should have, and actually stopped driving power down into every Welsh postcode which is what the vision to me really should always have been about - about people and places."

He said the party would accept its defeat and "come back stronger" with a "vision for a stronger Wales in a fairer United Kingdom."

Burnham said he wanted to achieve the sense of a "one Labour team for Wales" where the party is "pulling in the same direction".

"Where I'm pulling with you and not creating problems for you or going against what Ken or colleagues want to achieve.

"We will put forward a vision for communities up and down Wales, as well as giving Wales a stronger national voice."

News.title: Family's two-year fight to bring killer driver back from Latvia
News.content:
Days after her 12-year-old son was killed by a BMW driver travelling at 70mph, Louise Slater sat outside the suspect's home, gathering the courage to plead with his family to hand him in.

She had been given the name and address of Aleksanders Dolars after her son Keaton was killed in a hit-and-run in Coventry.

Distraught, she was preparing to knock on the door when a neighbour approached and asked what she was doing.

When she explained, he told her the family, from Latvia, had packed up and left a day or two earlier.

Keaton's suspected killer had fled just hours after leaving him dying in the road.

What followed was a relentless two-year fight by his parents to track him down and bring him back to England to face justice.

He was finally jailed on Friday, for nine years and four months.

This article contains upsetting details

Dolars' name had been already circulating locally before police identified him as their main suspect on 18 June 2024, four days after Keaton was killed.

A family waiting at nearby traffic lights said their seven-seater "shook violently" as a BMW driver sped past at what appeared to be far more than the 30mph limit. Moments later, they saw something fly into the air behind them.

The car did not stop.

As it disappeared from view, the family noticed a black rucksack and a single shoe lying in Radford Road and realised a child may have been hit.

News.title: Thousands turn out in Edinburgh to protest against AI data centres
News.content:
Thousands of people have joined a protest in Edinburgh against the building of large-scale AI data centres.

Demonstrators with placards - and some dressed in costume - assembled at the top of the Royal Mile before marching towards the Scottish Parliament.

The event comes at a time of widespread debate about the environmental impact of data centres and is part of a wave of protests across Europe.

The Scottish government will soon publish new planning guidance on data centres and said it was developing a strategy to maximise the "public benefit".

News.title: Milder weather coming before more cold health alerts take effect
News.content:
Another round of cold health alerts is set to come into force on Sunday following a brief break from the weekend's subzero temperatures.

After readings dipped as low as minus 7C early on Saturday, most places on Sunday morning will be milder and free of frost.

Widespread rainfall is likely with hail and thunderstorms possible for parts of Wales and southern England.

Into the new week, the wintry chill is set to return with UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) cold-health alerts beginning for the north-east and north-west of England and Yorkshire and the Humber from 21:00 GMT on Sunday.

News.title: Judge temporarily blocks Trump from moving ahead on Washington public golf course redevelopment
News.content:
Become an Independent member to bookmark this article Want to bookmark your favourite articles and stories to read or reference later? Start your Independent Membership today. Already a member? Log in

A federal judge on Saturday ordered a temporary stop to any work at a historic Washington public golf course not far from the White House, blocking for now President Donald Trump's push to redevelop the site along the Potomac River into a championship-level venue.

U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes issued the temporary restraining order before the East Potomac Golf Links was due to close Sunday for 15 months. Trump had announced work would begin that day despite the legal challenge initiated against the project in February by the DC Preservation League and two local golfers.

The plaintiffs argue that Trump's plan would change the character of the accessible golf course and make it unaffordable, something the Republican president denies. They had sought the stop-work order, saying that closing the course and launching work on the project would “irreparably injure plaintiffs and the public interest."

The park’s redevelopment is one of multiple projects in the nation's capital that Trump has championed to remake the city. They include a large memorial arch, a White House ballroom and the John F. Kennedy Center for the Performing Arts, among others.

Reyes had signaled throughout a five-hour court hearing Friday that she was likely to issue some stoppage for the park closure. The only issue was how expansive it might be. Justice Department lawyer Adam Gustafson argued that the entire East Potomac Park, which includes three golf courses, a miniature course, bike riding lanes and other recreational areas, was being closed because of safety factors. He also noted that the lease between the government and the current operator, National Links Trust, was ending Sunday.

Reyes pointed out that safety had not been part of the discussion over the closure for months and that ending the lease felt more like an action that provided a premise for the closure rather than an action that led to the closure of the course about 2 miles from the White House.

She also rejected Gustafson's argument that the closure was separate from Trump's repeated pronouncements that he wanted the course to be closed and renovated into a world-class venue and had called repeatedly for the park's closure by the deadline as part of what is known as the Washington National plan.

Even before the order, Trump lashed out in a social media post Saturday, contending that Reyes “doesn’t want us to quickly and inexpensively fix up the Course which is, also, very dangerous.” He said people who live in the Washington area would get a 50% discount on “any and all Rates charged” and that the redevelopment would “evolve into something very special, something which the Judge will be able to take great pride in seeing!”

Reyes’ order was the latest in a series of rulings in lawsuits challenging Trump’s projects that were issued just hours before construction was expected to begin. A different judge recently ordered a 14-day delay on work for the arch, a decision that came shortly after a key planning commission stacked with Trump appointees approved plans for the project.

Reyes, who was nominated to the court by Democratic President Joe Biden, had for months been reticent about approving the plaintiffs’ requests for work stoppages. The plaintiffs had argued the administration was moving ahead with work related to the project despite the pending lawsuit.

Her reluctance to issue orders ended in October, spurred in part by a tree-cutting spree by the administration over a holiday weekend with little notification to the judge or plaintiffs.

Officials and government lawyers said the tree work was part of a 2019 plan that recommended the cutting. In response, the judge confronted the administration over what she portrayed as deceitful actions over its intentions for the project.

Reyes has repeatedly expressed frustration over the minute planning details she has been asked to adjudicate, including over the trees being cut down at the 106-year-old park. The Justice Department filed a request that Reyes be removed from the case because of what it called her “egregious behavior” and questioned her impartiality. Reyes has not recused herself.

The restraining order was one of two issues Reyes took up during Friday's hearing.

She announced plans last week to name Jessie Liu, a former U.S. attorney for the District of Columbia, to examine whether officials with the Interior Department and the National Park Service and attorneys with the Justice Department had violated ethics or misled her during the course of the case. Gustafson asked her to reconsider and give the Justice Department the opportunity to show an outside investigator was unnecessary.

“It's quite a cloud on the people it affects,” he said.

Reyes said she understood.

“To be frank with you I don’t want to do this,” she said, but she had an ethical obligation to at least look because "I think there is enough smoke that someone needs to consider whether there’s been fire.”
