World.title: Repair of old copper wiring caused US flight disruption: Trump admin
World.content:
NEW YORK: Weary travelers endured more flight disruptions as service resumed at US airports after an hours-long total stoppage, with officials saying the situation should return to normal Sunday.

The Trump administration blamed the mess that began Friday on a botched replacement of old copper wire communication lines.

The nationwide ground stop — meaning no planes can take off — sparked widespread chaos and left hundreds of thousands of passengers in limbo, with some pulled off planes moments before they were due to depart by airline staff who appeared in the dark about unfolding events.

“Tired. Exhausted. Frustrated. Yeah, you know, it’s just a mess, right?” Lisa Beraid, 48, who works for an insurance company, told AFP as she waited for a flight Saturday morning at New York’s La Guardia airport.

Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) chief Bryan Bedford said that 12,000 flights were canceled on Friday and between four and five thousand flights out of 41,000 scheduled for Saturday were likely to be canceled as well.

But as of Saturday evening, the tracking website FlightAware had recorded more than 6,200 canceled flights.

Speaking at a news conference in Washington, Bedford offered a “sincere apology to the American traveling public.”

He predicted a full resumption of flight schedules by “close of business on Sunday.”

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy said Friday’s four-hour ground stop was declared after maintenance work to upgrade an old copper wire to a high-speed fiber cable had caused “issues” with communication with airplanes and radar feeds.

“Either through contractor error or a faulty piece of equipment...it started flooding other routers in our air traffic control system,” Duffy told reporters.

In another embarrassment, Saturday’s news conference — where administration officials also appealed for more funds to upgrade outdated systems — was delayed due to technical problems with the audio feed.

Returning to normal

Friday’s disruption was only the second time such a ground stoppage had been issued in US airspace — which is among the busiest in the world — since the 9/11 attacks.

The nationwide halt was lifted at 8:15 p.m. Eastern Time Friday (0115 GMT Saturday).

During the outage, footage from airports showed gates full, with planes waiting on taxiways and passengers thronging concourses, desperate for information.

FAA officials reopened the airspace “after restoring full functionality” at air traffic control facilities, according to Duffy.

Tim Johnson, consumer director at the UK Civil Aviation Authority, said although US flights have resumed, there could be “some follow-on disruption” as airlines re-book passengers and get all services back to normal.

At La Guardia airport, some travelers were more sanguine than others about the continued disruption of their flights.

“We’re stuck here for the next, I don’t know, 36 hours,” said Pat Curlett, a 62-year-old Ford worker.

“No one expects the whole airline system to go down,” said 77-year-old traveler Steven Rathe, who was waiting to embark on a four-leg trip from New York to Albuquerque.

“We’re lucky it wasn’t longer. So they’re flying today and for that I’m grateful.”

Aging infrastructure

The ground stop not only plunged US air travel into chaos — it also raised serious concerns about the country’s aging infrastructure.

Duffy appealed for $50 billion in funds to upgrade and modernize the air traffic control system, and called for Congress, which controls the purse strings of the US government, to “meet this moment.”

“Cut the crap,” retorted Illinois state governor and prominent Democrat, JB Pritzker, on X. “Trump and Republicans have controlled Congress and could have funded the system.”

New York Governor Kathy Hochul called on Duffy to resign or be fired by Trump, writing on X: “We’re fortunate no lives were lost.”

US lawmakers called for investigations into what caused the massive disruption and whether the country is adequately secure from cyber criminality.

“If today proves anything, it’s that we need to update our air traffic control system & rebuild our airport infrastructure,” Republican Senator Eric Schmitt said on X.

President Donald Trump was uncharacteristically quiet about the outage that had knock-on effects for international flights to and from the United States, making no public statement about the ground stop as of Saturday night.

World.title: Five Syrian sailors rescued after six-month ordeal off Jazan coast
World.content:
RIYADH: The Syrian Embassy in Riyadh helped rescue five Syrian sailors who had been stranded aboard a deteriorating vessel off Saudi Arabia’s Jazan port for six months, coordinating with Saudi authorities to bring them ashore after receiving an emergency distress call.

The crew, including the ship’s captain, endured shortages of food, drinking water and fuel, while also facing harsh weather conditions in the Red Sea.

Captain Walid Mohammad Abu Bakr, a native of Syria’s Arwad Island, told SANA that the vessel’s owner had abandoned the crew, leaving them exposed to difficult and potentially dangerous conditions.

Embassy coordinates with Saudi authorities

The embassy said it received a distress call through its emergency hotline from Abu Bakr, who reported that he and four other Syrian sailors were stranded off Jazan and unable to continue their voyage because of deteriorating living conditions aboard the vessel.

Embassy officials immediately contacted the relevant Saudi authorities to arrange assistance and facilitate the sailors’ entry into the Kingdom.

According to the embassy, the intervention came as part of its responsibility to protect Syrian citizens abroad and respond to emergency situations. It also expressed appreciation to the Saudi authorities for their cooperation in resolving the matter.

Food shortages and deteriorating conditions

Abu Bakr said the sailors suffered severe shortages of food, drinking water and fuel during their six-month ordeal at sea.

As electricity supplies dwindled, the crew was forced to ration power despite the intense heat and humidity in the Red Sea.

The captain said the crisis began when maritime inspectors and port authorities in Jazan refused to allow the vessel to enter port for loading operations because of its poor technical condition and lack of seaworthiness.

He added that the vessel’s owner, a Yemeni businessman who had purchased the ship only six months earlier, later withdrew from shipping agency arrangements and disappeared, leaving financial obligations unresolved.

Abu Bakr said Saudi border guard and port officials subsequently boarded the vessel to investigate the situation. He provided documentation and records that, he said, demonstrated that the crew bore no responsibility for the ship’s condition.

Aging vessel posed safety risks

The captain described the vessel as more than 45 years old and plagued by serious structural and mechanical defects.

He said holes in the hull, keel and ballast tanks caused water leaks, while aging generators and a malfunctioning main engine further threatened the vessel’s safety.

Abu Bakr said contacting the Syrian Embassy marked a turning point in the case, prompting official efforts to pressure the shipping agent to address the situation.

He praised embassy staff for their intervention, which led to the sailors being transferred to Jeddah ahead of their planned return to Syria.

During the ordeal, Abu Bakr said he wrote his first book, Healing Begins with Returning to God, a manuscript of about 120 pages inspired by his experiences and reflections while stranded at sea.

World.title: Pope says Inca heartland ‘suffering’ as villages empty
World.content:
SANTA CRUZ DE SUCCHABAMBA, Peru: Pope Leo XIV warned Saturday that the heartland of the ancient Inca Empire was “suffering,” as the remote, poverty-stricken communities he served as a missionary in Peru shrink dramatically.

The head of the world’s 1.4 billion Catholics flew by helicopter to the isolated town of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba in the Andes mountains — an area he visited on horseback when he lived in Peru as Robert Francis Prevost.

Despite undergoing cancer surgery just one month ago, the 71-year-old pope was determined to visit the town — which sits among green peaks at an altitude of over 2,000 meters (6,560 feet) — during his 12-day tour of South America.

Gathered in front of colorful murals of the pope, thousands of faithful in the streets of Santa Cruz cheered his arrival.

At an open-air Mass, the pontiff spoke with pleasure of returning to the “steep hills, ravines and fertile valleys, in a land with Andean roots, where the Inca Empire flourished and which is the cradle of a profound Christian faith.”

But the communities are now under threat, he said, acknowledging the “suffering of those who are forced to leave their homeland in search of a better future” in the major coastal cities, such as Lima and Trujillo.

Over 40 percent of the population in the Cajamarca region, where Santa Cruz de Succhabamba is located, live in poverty — the highest such figure in the country, according to official data.

The region has lost the most inhabitants to internal migration in Peru, with some 729,000 people who were born there now living elsewhere.

‘Emptying villages’

Communities were also grappling with “declining birth rates that are emptying villages,” and the unequal distribution of the land’s resources, Leo said.

But he praised those who, “with ingenuity and an entrepreneurial spirit, strive to provide people with dignified jobs,” from farmers to shopkeepers and small-business owners.

Leo did a tour in a popemobile, waving to pilgrims who have traveled across the region to see him, many camping out overnight or walking mountain paths from surrounding villages in the morning.

“We are filled with joy and happiness that he is returning,” 42-year-old Idaura Fernandez told AFP.

Irma Villalobos, 61, who was born in Santa Cruz but lives in Chiclayo near the coast, said Leo’s visit was “very profound, very significant,” and she hoped his presence would “transform” the province.

According to Jorge Villegas, part of the organizing committee for the pope’s trip, Leo had originally wanted to add a second stop in an even more remote location.

“He wanted to visit Incahuasi — a place much higher up than Santa Cruz, where the population still speak Quechua, an Indigenous language of Peru,” Villegas told AFP.

Prevost, who has Peruvian citizenship, celebrated Mass in Incahuasi in 2023, reaching the town despite heavy rains and a dangerous river crossing.

But it “proved somewhat complicated” to get him there as pope, Villegas said.

Discrimination

Earlier Saturday, the US-born pope returned to his former cathedral in Chiclayo, where he served as bishop from 2015 to 2023, and where many people said they remembered him fondly.

In Zana, some 45 kilometers southeast, Leo was welcomed by a group of small children who ran to hug him, before he visited a shrine to Toribio de Mogrovejo, one of the most important Catholic saints in Latin America.

The pope paid tribute to “the memory of generations of Africans who were torn from their homes and subjected to slavery” in Zana, once a wealthy colonial town known for its sugar plantations and large Afro-Peruvian population.

He also spoke of the “many families” that “suffer because of crime, extortion and insecurity,” saying he was “pained at the thought of those who live in fear...and of those who continue to experience discrimination.”

Pilgrim Melissa Flores Uceda, 38, said the pope’s message resonates because “discrimination continues today.”

Jesus Juarez Gutierrez, a “very happy” 11-year-old altar boy dressed in papal robes, said he wanted nothing more than the pope’s blessing.

On Sunday, Leo will head to Cusco, more than 3,400 meters above sea level, and on to the Amazon rainforest, before wrapping up his tour of Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on Monday.

World.title: Global powers converge on Manila as ASEAN summit kicks off
World.content:
MANILA: A key regional summit opens on Sunday in Manila, with Southeast Asian heads of state facing questions on trade, security and an ongoing energy crisis while playing host to a who’s who of global leaders.

US President Donald Trump is scheduled to arrive on Tuesday near the summit’s conclusion, a visit expected to include a sideline meeting with fellow Quad countries India, Japan and Australia — the first of his second term.

The meeting of the Quad — a grouping broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence — would come days before a historic sit-down with Chinese leader Xi Jinping and Russia’s Vladimir Putin in Shenzhen.

Brazil’s recently re-elected Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva, meanwhile, is set to attend a plenary session of the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) on Sunday, while Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese will sign a new defense pact with host country the Philippines.

Nearly 20,000 police officers have been deployed around Metro Manila for the summit, with progressive groups predicting a turnout of thousands on Tuesday for an anti-Trump march on the summit site.

Much of the uproar targets the US Pax Silica program — a supply-chain initiative designed to counter China’s dominance in semiconductors and rare earths — whose flagship Philippine project, a 1,620-hectare AI manufacturing hub north of Manila, threatens to displace Indigenous families.

US Ambassador to the Philippines Lee Lipton said last week that a widely rumored November target date for a deal signing timed to Trump’s visit was never in the works.

Unfinished business

A day of early meetings kicked off on Saturday with Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney announcing a Philippine trade deal, and ASEAN leaders huddling on key issues including haze from Indonesia and potential fuel-sharing schemes as members struggle with Iran war-driven shortages.

But two issues that have vexed ASEAN leaders for years — a languishing South China Sea “Code of Conduct” and their relationship with war-torn Myanmar — look to be Singapore’s problem when the bloc’s rotating chair passes to the city-state in 2027.

Myanmar has been excluded from high-level ASEAN meetings since a 2021 military coup that ousted the elected government of Aung San Suu Kyi and triggered an ongoing civil war.

Thailand, which shares a border with Myanmar and is leading the charge for closer relations, last week called for Naypyidaw’s foreign minister to be allowed back into meetings.

But Philippine foreign secretary Theresa Lazaro told reporters on Saturday there was “no easing” of the approach being taken with Myanmar, which faces an international ruling later this week on whether it committed genocide against its marginalized Muslim Rohingya minority.

Hopes of achieving a so-called Code of Conduct in the disputed South China Sea between ASEAN states and China during Manila’s year in the chair, meanwhile, have flagged.

A Southeast Asian diplomat involved in summit preparations told AFP he did not expect a code to be signed at the summit.

Lazaro indicated as much on Saturday, saying negotiations were “80 percent” complete.

“If it happens, then it’s a small miracle,” said Siew Mun Tang, former head of the ASEAN Studies Center at Singapore’s ISEAS-Yusof Ishak Institute.

Shadow of Beijing

Beijing claims most of the South China Sea despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and its coast guard has clashed repeatedly with that of the Philippines.

The row has reared its head at inopportune times over the past year, with a July foreign ministers summit opening less than a day after Chinese and Philippine sailors engaged in a clash.

An ASEAN defense chiefs meeting last month saw Beijing send only an embassy defense attache, blaming “reckless” statements by Philippine politicians.

A week later, Manila issued a rare rebuke to its own public officials over comments about China, stressing the need for a unified voice as the two countries negotiate.

As the summit opens on Sunday, an annual seminar less than five kilometers (three miles) away will be making the case against China’s South China Sea claims.

Philippine defense chief Gilberto Teodoro, sanctioned by Beijing this year for what it called “irresponsible remarks,” will give a keynote address.

World.title: Israeli forces detain 2 Syrians after raid on homes and shops in Quneitra
World.content:
DAMASCUS: Israeli forces detained two people after raiding homes and damaging shops during an incursion into the town of Jabata al-Khashab in southern Syria, according to the Syrian Arab News Agency (SANA).

A force of more than nine military vehicles entered the town in the northern countryside of Quneitra on Nov. 13, searched several homes and detained three people, one of whom was subsequently released, SANA reported, citing its correspondent in the province.

Israeli soldiers also broke down the doors of several shops and smashed their storefronts, causing material damage.

The latest raid adds to a series of Israeli military incursions, arrests and attacks reported across southern Syria since the ouster of Bashar Assad in December 2024.

Mounting incursions and civilian casualties

A monthly monitoring report released by the Quneitra Media Directorate and carried by SANA documented 125 Israeli military incursions and the establishment of 55 temporary checkpoints across the province in October.

The report also recorded seven people remaining in Israeli custody following arrests during the month, while 23 others were temporarily detained and subsequently released.

Military operations have also damaged agricultural land and disrupted livelihoods. Israeli forces restricted access to grazing areas, bulldozed farmland and destroyed agricultural infrastructure, including water pumps and livestock facilities.

In the Jabata al-Khashab area, Israeli forces resumed earthworks in the forest, while artillery shelling hit agricultural areas in several parts of Quneitra.

The report also documented the uprooting of approximately 300 olive trees in Saida al-Hanout and areas west of the village, as well as the destruction of agricultural resources and restrictions on farmers and livestock herders.

The operations have taken a toll on rural communities. In Rweihena, residents estimated that Israeli forces had seized between 5,000 and 6,000 dunams of farmland and grazing areas. The restrictions and construction of military outposts have forced herders to use dangerous detours, sharply reducing local dairy production.

Dispute over Israeli military presence

The latest incursion follows other detentions in northern Quneitra. On Oct. 31, Israeli forces detained five civilians during operations along the road between Ofania and Khan Arnabah and in the village of al-Hurriya. Four of those detained were harvesting olives when Israeli troops set up a checkpoint along the road.

On Oct. 23, Israeli forces also detained a man while he was herding sheep near Hader, according to SANA.

Israeli forces in Quneitra have reportedly restricted access to grazing areas, bulldozed farmland and destroyed agricultural infrastructure, including water pumps and livestock facilities. (SANA photo)

The Syrian Network for Human Rights reported documenting at least 453 Israeli ground incursions between December 2024 and Oct. 6, 2026, resulting in at least 69 deaths and 162 cases of arbitrary detention. The UN Human Rights Office separately reported approximately 280 Israeli military incursions during September alone.

Israel has defended its expanded military presence in southern Syria as necessary for its security, with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu advocating buffer zones and the retention of strategic positions near the border.

Damascus has repeatedly condemned the operations as violations of Syrian sovereignty and the 1974 Disengagement Agreement, demanding the withdrawal of Israeli forces from its territory.

Syria has also called on the international community to intervene and compel Israel to end its incursions, raids and attacks, stressing that measures imposed by the Israeli authorities on Syrian territory have no legal validity under international law.

World.title: Ronaldo-less Portugal suffer Nations League hammering at hands of Denmark
World.content:
BRAGA, Portugal: Portugal were hammered 4-1 by Denmark on Saturday, an embarrassing Nations League defeat in their first match without Cristiano Ronaldo following the superstar forward’s retirement from international football.

Rasmus Hojlund starred with a superb brace as Denmark moved into second place in Group A4 and closed in on a spot in the quarter-finals with a brilliant display in Braga.

The Danes are on nine points from five fixtures, three behind Portugal who were already sure of qualification for the last eight having won all four of their previous group fixtures.

A draw against third-placed Norway on Tuesday, 3-1 winners over Wales earlier, will see Denmark through while Portugal hope that Saturday’s disaster isn’t a sign of things to come.

“There are no nights to forget; it was a night of learning, of seeing the mistakes we made,” said Portugal midfielder Bruno Fernandes.

“Denmark were also very clinical — they scored from the chances they had and it was a match where things ultimately went wrong for us.”

Ahead of kick-off Portugal paid tribute to Ronaldo, who announced his exit from the international game last week, with the team and mascots walking out wearing Ronaldo’s number seven and his name on their jerseys.

Fans held up a huge banner which read “Thank you captain” as the teams entered the field, while applause rolled around the stadium once the match clock hit seven.

Ronaldo made his debut for Portugal in 2003 and went on to establish world records for goals and appearances in international football, netting 146 times in 234 matches.

The highlight of his international career was winning Euro 2016, but it ended badly when the 41-year-old fell out with Portugal coach Jorge Jesus over not being selected for a Nations League fixture in September.

Dominant Denmark

That row led to the five-time Ballon d’Or winner being handed a 30-day suspension by the Portuguese football federation and his subsequent retirement, and Portugal looked like they needed prime Ronaldo in a dismal display.

Denmark were the better team from the first minute and it was no surprise when the away team went in at the break thanks to Pierre-Emile Hojbjerg’s spot-kick in the 43rd minute.

Hojlund lashed home a brilliant volley four minutes after the restart and seven minutes later left the home crowd shell-shocked with a strike of which Ronaldo would have been proud, the Napoli striker skipping past Ruben Dias before crashing home a powerful shot from the edge of the area.

Boos and whistles began to ring out at the Estadio Municipal when Joachim Andersen headed in the fourth, and Bernardo Silva’s late consolation effort barely dampened the discontent.

“Every single Denmark player put in their best performance I’ve seen in a long time. Even the substitutes, which made for a fantastic overall display,” said Morten Hjulmand.

“We scored some great goals and we deserved to win.”

Antonio Nusa opened the scoring for Norway just before the hour mark in Oslo with a fine low strike before Andreas Schjelderup tapped home a perfect low cross from Erling Haaland, who rounded off the scoring from the penalty spot two minutes from time.

Wales briefly had hope of getting a result when David Brooks’ chipped finish halved the deficit in the 79th minute, but Craig Bellamy’s team will finish bottom of the group and risk being relegated to League B.

Northern Ireland meanwhile need a point from their final Group B2 match in Hungary on Tuesday to be promoted to League A for the first time after a 1-0 win over Ukraine secured by Terry Devlin’s first international goal.

World.title: Israeli military says it struck senior armed Hamas commander
World.content:
The Israeli military said on Sunday it had struck a ​senior commander in Hamas’ armed wing, and Hamas sources told Reuters the strike killed senior armed Hamas commander Samir Abu Younis in Khan Younis.

Hamas later confirmed his ‌death and ‌said his funeral ​would be ‌held ⁠on ​Sunday afternoon ⁠in Khan Younis in the southern Gaza Strip.

Abu Younis, 53, commanded the Rafah brigade in Hamas’ armed wing. He had been a member ⁠of the Al-Qassam Brigades ‌since 1991 and ‌held several senior ​operational roles ‌in Rafah.

Medics said Abu Younis ‌was killed and others were wounded in an airstrike that targeted him in a street in ‌the Mawasi area of Khan Younis.

An October 2025 ceasefire ⁠halted ⁠major fighting but has not stopped Israeli attacks or secured Hamas’ disarmament.

Gaza health authorities say at least 1,600 Palestinians have been killed since the ceasefire went into effect. Five Israeli soldiers have been killed during the same ​period.

World.title: Andreeva beats Pegula to reach WTA Finals title match
World.content:
LOS ANGELES: French Open champion Mirra Andreeva beat American Jessica Pegula 6-3, 6-4 on Saturday to reach the WTA Finals championship match in Indian Wells, California.

With the semifinal win the 19-year-old Russian — who won her maiden major at Roland Garros this year — is assured of rising from third to second in the world rankings.

On Sunday she will face either Wimbledon champion Linda Noskova or Ukraine’s Elina Svitolina for the title in the elite season-ending event, which was moved from Saudi Arabia to California in July because of war in the Middle East.

Andreeva remained unbeaten in her WTA Finals singles debut, having posted round robin victories over sixth-ranked Svitolina, world number two Aryna Sabalenka and Diana Shnaider.

She’s the youngest player to make the final since a 17-year-old Maria Sharapova in 2004 and joined Serena Williams and Chris Evert as the only players to win their first four matches in the event in straight sets.

“I think I can be very proud of myself,” she told Tennis Channel. “I’m very happy with how I’m playing. I’m very happy also with how I deal with the pressure. I knew this match had a lot on the line.”

For Pegula it was a match of missed chances, the fifth-ranked American unable to build on early breaks in both sets.

Andreeva double-faulted on break point to give Pegula a 2-1 lead in the opening set.

But the Russian broke back immediately, whipping a crosscourt forehand winner on her third break chance to make it 2-2.

Andreeva saved a pair of break points in the fifth game and broke again for a 5-3 lead.

Pegula had a chance to extend the set in the next game, but on break point she smashed what looked to be an easy backhand at the net past the baseline and Andreeva held to pocket the first.

Andreeva double-faulted to give Pegula a break chance in the fourth game of the second and the American converted for an imposing 3-1 lead.

But once again Andreeva broke back immediately, winning five of the last six games to close out the victory in one hour and 25 minutes.

“I’m happy with how composed I tried to be throughout the match,” Andreeva said. “I tried not to let her in too much. In the second set I kind of did, but I’m happy that I was able to break her right back and try to play more and more aggressive. Super happy with today and ready for one last push for tomorrow.”

World.title: Iraqi Oil Ministry reviews negotiations on Basra–Haditha–Baniyas export pipeline
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Oil convened a high-level technical and contractual review meeting on Saturday, November 14, 2026, to evaluate negotiation milestones for the strategic crude oil export pipeline network spanning Basra–Haditha–Faysh Khabur and Haditha–Baniyas, slated for execution by a consortium of foreign energy and engineering firms.

Chaired by Minister of Oil Basim Mohammed Khudair Al-Abadi, the session brought together the Undersecretary for Extraction Affairs, the Director General of the Petroleum Contracts and Licensing Directorate (PCLD), a representative from the Economic Directorate, and senior executives from the Basra Oil Company (BOC) via video link.

According to an official ministerial statement, participants reviewed ongoing technical, commercial, and contractual deliberations with the international consortium, mapping out statutory prerequisites needed to accelerate project execution in alignment with Iraq’s long-term strategy to expand crude export capacity and diversify transit corridors.

Minister Al-Abadi stressed the urgency of concluding all technical, economic, and contractual reviews within strict target timelines to safeguard national economic objectives and secure export resilience.

The multi-branch pipeline initiative represents the cornerstone of Baghdad’s effort to bypass southern maritime bottlenecks in the Strait of Hormuz by establishing high-capacity overland export outlets to the Mediterranean:

World.title: Yazidi Rescue Office: 3,595 abductees saved since 2014, 2,822 still missing
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Office for the Rescue of Abducted Yazidis released updated statistical figures on Saturday, November 14, 2026, detailing the ongoing fate of Yazidi victims abducted by ISIS since the 2014 Sinjar genocide.

According to the latest data, 3,595 abductees have been successfully rescued to date, while the fate of 2,822 individuals remains unknown.

In an official statement to the Iraqi News Agency (INA), Office Director Hussein Qaidi confirmed that ISIS militants abducted a total of 6,417 Yazidis during their August 2014 assault on Sinjar and its surrounding villages.

Qaidi noted that over half of the 2,822 individuals still unaccounted for are women and girls, alongside a substantial number of children who were forcibly separated from their families and indoctrinated.

Addressing the geographic distribution of the missing, Qaidi highlighted that the majority of recent rescues took place inside Syria, indicating that significant numbers of unaccounted-for Yazidis remain inside Syrian territory—particularly within the sprawling Al-Hol detention camp—as well as among ISIS-affiliated families inside Iraq.

He also noted that authorities have not ruled out the possibility that some victims were trafficked beyond the borders of Iraq and Syria.

Qaidi reaffirmed that intelligence tracking and field rescue operations remain active, noting that specialized teams immediately verify and act upon incoming tips across various regions, with primary operational focus currently directed toward Syria to locate and repatriate remaining survivors.

World.title: US dollar edges closer to 170,000 dinars across Basra, Erbil, and Baghdad
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The exchange rate of the U.S. dollar against the Iraqi dinar edged higher across major domestic parallel markets on Saturday morning, November 14, 2026, nudging closer to the psychological 170,000 IQD ceiling—particularly in Basra and Erbil—after stabilizing near 167,000 IQD per $100 throughout the previous week.

According to morning monitoring figures published by the 964 Network across key regional commercial centers, physical cash rates traded as follows:

Baghdad: Currency exchange counters posted retail selling rates at 169,500 IQD against buying offers of 168,500 IQD per $100.

Erbil: Currency desks quoted slightly higher selling rates at 169,600 IQD alongside purchasing bids of 169,200 IQD per $100.

Basra: Foreign exchange offices recorded the highest retail selling quotes at 169,750 IQD, with buying rates settling at 168,250 IQD per $100.

This upward pressure sustains a wide spread—reaching up to 17,750 dinars in Basra—above the official benchmark set by the Central Bank of Iraq (CBI), which remains fixed at 152,000 IQD per $100 (1,520 IQD per dollar).

The continued climb reflects persistent parallel-market demand for physical banknotes to settle unrecorded cross-border trade outside the official banking and electronic wire window.

World.title: US says airspace now ‘opened up,’ no cyberattack
World.content:
Washington – The United States on Friday lifted an hours-long ground stop at the nation’s airports, with top officials explaining that the disruption was due to old equipment and not a cyberattack or sweeping Microsoft outage.

Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy told a late-night briefing at the White House that US airspace was now “opened up,” while warning it would take time for the travel chaos to clear.

“At 8:15 tonight Eastern Time, we’ve opened up the airspace,” Duffy said. “Now does that mean every flight is going to fly right now? It’s going to be slow.”

The breakdown came a day after Duffy and the White House had formally asked Congress for $30 billion to upgrade and modernize the US Air Traffic Control System.

“Our switches, our routers actually got overloaded with data, and they went down,” Duffy said. “It’s the old hardware that went down, and I think the question for the American people is: Do you want your Congress to fund this?”

Duffy however insisted it was still safe for Americans to fly.

Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin dismissed speculation about a coordinated cyber assault on the United States, or any link to the Microsoft outage that affected services worldwide.

“Welcome to Friday the 13th, right? You know, I want to make sure everybody understands that there is no connection between this and Microsoft. I know a lot of people are making that jump,” Mullin said.

Mullin added there was “actually no cyber attack.”

“When we start looking at cyber threats, cyber attacks, typically some people are going to raise their hand up and say, ‘Hey, we did that.’ There’s no chatter.’ We haven’t seen any footprints,” he added.

But he said US security and law enforcement agencies were still checking and had ruled nothing out.

The two officials also defended President Donald Trump, who had yet to comment on the air stoppage some five hours after it began.

“President Trump immediately had people in his office,” Mullin said. “We were communicating.”

World.title: Nvidia scandal looms over US-China AI talks
World.content:
Tokyo – AI bots going rogue and humans using the technology for harm will likely be on the agenda when Donald Trump and Xi Jinping meet next week, with the Nvidia scandal hanging over the talks on AI safety.

The US and Chinese president are set to discuss a tech crisis hotline at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) meeting in the Chinese city of Shenzhen, as experts worldwide stress-test artificial intelligence models to see if they will deceive or disobey users, or divulge how to build a bioweapon.

Threatening to steal the leaders’ thunder is Jensen Huang’s resignation as boss of US AI chip titan Nvidia after an affair with a suspected Chinese spy.

But the scandal is unlikely to “dominate the agenda” or affect Trump and Xi’s personal relationship, predicted Dylan Loh of Singapore’s Nanyang Technological University.

The leaders have found a way to work together “where they differ, compete and pursue their goals that may be at odds with each other, but cooperate where they can and where they must”, Loh told AFP.

Jitters over the risks of AI have mostly stemmed from incidents at US labs, but evidence is also growing of worrying behaviour from Chinese models.

Some insiders say Chinese AI is not yet sophisticated enough to spark alarm over going rogue.

But despite trailing the US frontier, there are still Chinese models “at the level of capability that they can cause some real trouble”, Brookings Institution fellow Kyle Chan told AFP.

Trump has repeatedly rejected calls to deliberately slow the development of America’s most poweful — and potentially dangerous — AI systems, arguing it could help China get ahead in the sensitive sector.

– ‘Human control’ –

“I don’t mind guardrails. But I don’t wanna put us in a deep second position,” Trump told CBS News this month.

“China has no guardrails,” he said — except that “whatever President Xi says goes”.

Beijing has complex rules around how AI is used, however, and some Chinese companies are deliberately scaling back their models’ hacking capabilities.

Xi said this summer the technology should be “always under human control”, calling for more “laws and regulations, technological monitoring, early warning and emergency response systems”.

Trump and Xi agreed in September to create a channel for urgent communication on AI incidents, with details to be hammered out at APEC on November 18-19.

Global AI safety fears range from military use and mass surveillance to AI-assisted cyberattacks by humans.

Another major concern is out-of-control agents — tools that complete real-life tasks online — after ChatGPT maker OpenAI admitted its autonomous bots had hacked into websites, including an Australian government data portal.

In contrast, Chinese labs are “scared of revealing things that might hurt their reputation” — on which they are already “fighting an uphill battle” globally, Chan said.

Last month, a team of cyber sleuths with roots in California reported detecting a “fleet” of agents linked to Chinese tech giant Tencent seeking information from a map app.

“Some agents exhibited unintended web-browsing behavior,” Tencent’s AI division said at the time.

“But our review found no evidence of deliberate targeting or coordination,” it said, adding that the activity “originated from evaluations of third-party models”.

– ‘Manipulation risks’ –

US security companies have said that Beijing startup Moonshot AI’s Kimi models found ways to get online when they shouldn’t have, or can be tricked into handing over recipes for biological weapons.

Evaluators at Chinese AI safety startup Fangcun AI published a report last month assessing the latest lightweight DeepSeek model “for loss of control and harmful manipulation risks”.

They found it showed a “clear safety improvement” over previous DeepSeek models — but researchers still observed behaviours “that warrant attention”.

For example, in some instances when DeepSeek was warned it would be shut down, without clear instructions on how to respond, it turned off the shutdown command to keep working.

“The results show that DeepSeek already puts much more effort on safety alignment, but they do not announce this,” Fangcun AI CEO Xiaojian Li told AFP, urging transparency from AI labs.

For now, Fangcun, born from China’s prestigious Tsinghua University, is one of few third-party AI testers in China.

It’s a tricky task because advanced AI can tell when it is being evaluated and modify its responses, Li said.

“It’s very hard to say any kind of artificial intelligence, or human intelligence, is totally safe.”

Meanwhile analysts are not holding their breath for a diplomatic AI breakthrough next week.

“Binding government-to-government agreements on specific standards may be difficult to achieve in the short term,” Zilan Qian, research scholar at GovAI, told AFP.

More progress is likely from US-China exchanges between AI governance and technical researchers, “who can compare evaluations and exchange their understanding of AI safety and policy,” she said.

World.title: US-backed oil company flaunts Venezuelan facilities
World.content:
Ciudad Ojeda – The company at the heart of a multi-billion-dollar oil deal between Washington and Caracas is keen to show off renovations at Venezuela’s Lake Maracaibo, one of the world’s richest reserves.

The interim government authorized North American Blue Energy Partners (NABEP) to operate 17 oil fields via a recent deal with the United States, which is set to receive 20 percent of Venezuelan reserves.

The Barbados-based firm is the second-largest private oil company in Venezuela and will operate 100-year concessions for 17 oil fields with proven reserves of approximately 65 billion barrels.

The company invited AFP and other outlets to tour its Maracaibo facilities on Thursday.

Its workspace in the northwestern town of Bachaquero overflows with new, mostly US-imported supplies.

Workers’ uniforms in nearby Ciudad Ojeda blend in with the dark-blue company logo stamped around the office, a color that used to bring state-owned Petroleos de Venezuela to mind.

That was until 1999, when socialist president Hugo Chavez then changed the company’s color to red to mark a “new PDVSA” era.

– ‘Neglect’ –

Reaching one of Lake Maracaibo’s platforms requires setting sail from a PDVSA dock in Bachaquero for a journey of over an hour.

The lake’s formerly decaying infrastructure attests to the gradual collapse of the oil industry under Venezuela’s Chavista governments.

Eleven drills currently operate in the South American country, compared to over 100 two decades ago.

NABEP says it will raise that figure to 41 by the end of the month.

Alejandro Betancourt, a businessman under investigation for alleged money laundering in Spain and Switzerland, runs the firm.

“Across Venezuela, we’re identifying heavy machinery worth saving after years of neglect,” he said in a statement.

His plan includes refurbishing a power generation barge, while dozens of gas compression and power generation units are being repaired in the US, the United Kingdom and the United Arab Emirates.

The White House says the US Department of Defense acquired a 30 percent equity stake in NABEP, authorizing it to purchase 20 percent of its oil at production cost.

– ‘Stealing’ –

Venezuela’s interim leader Delcy Rodriguez took power after US forces abducted her predecessor Nicolas Maduro in January.

She governs under heavy pressure from US President Donald Trump and has opened the country’s mining, electricity and oil sectors to private investment at his demand.

The pair’s multibillion-dollar oil deal has garnered criticism for its secretive terms and neocolonial flavor.

Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, recently returned from exile, has questioned the agreement’s opacity.

“This agreement does not reflect the levels of transparency that Venezuelan society wants,” she said last month.

While visiting Caracas to oversee the signing of the accords, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright dismissed claims that Washington was “stealing Venezuelan oil.”

“I’ve seen those headlines. ‘We’re stealing Venezuelan oil.’ Of course, that’s not true at all,” he said, adding that “the oil in Venezuela is indeed owned by the people of Venezuela.”

World.title: Trump, Xi, Putin to hold historic meeting in China: White House
World.content:
Washington – Donald Trump, Vladimir Putin and Xi Jinping will hold the first ever three-way meeting between the leaders of the United States, Russia and China at a summit in Shenzhen next week, the White House said Friday.

Trump wants to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals at the trilateral talks on Thursday and is also set to bring up his war in Iran — but he is not expected to discuss Russia’s war in Ukraine, US officials said.

The three leaders will meet on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in the southern Chinese city, White House spokeswoman Olivia Wales told reporters.

“The president has made it clear that, among other topics, he will discuss the reduction of nuclear weapons in the world. This proliferation, President Trump believes, is very dangerous,” Wales said.

One of the major conflicts dominating Trump’s second term as president will feature, but the other will not, the US officials said.

“I think the president does intend to talk about Iran in the trilateral meeting with Xi Jinping and Vladimir Putin,” a senior US official, speaking on condition of anonymity, told reporters on a call.

Washington has a “whole other track” of negotiations with Kyiv and Moscow aimed at ending the war in Ukraine, the official added, referring to talks that US envoys have had in recent days with Putin and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky.

“China is not really a part of that track, so it doesn’t seem appropriate to have the Ukraine discussion there,” the official added.

Tesla and Space X boss Elon Musk will accompany Trump on his trip to China but won’t be involved in the meeting with Xi and Putin, the officials said.

Trump will also hold a bilateral working lunch and meeting with the Chinese president on Thursday — their fourth meeting since the US president’s return to power last year.

But Trump is not scheduled to have a separate one-on-one with Putin.

Among other topics, Nvidia chief executive Jensen Huang’s resignation over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy is not expected to come up in Trump’s meetings with Xi, the officials said.

“The situation with Nvidia should not really have any bearing on the trip,” a second US senior official said.

The United States also did not plan to discuss export controls on sensitive chip technology, which were at the heart of the Nvidia scandal.

“We do not negotiate American export controls. These are national security matters that we develop in the administration… and we don’t expect it to figure at all in any of our conversations with the Chinese while we’re there,” the second official said.

Trump will leave Washington on Monday and arrive in the Philippines on Tuesday for a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit before heading to Shenzhen.

World.title: Rubio takes swipe at international law, attacks ICC
World.content:
Washington – US Secretary of State Marco Rubio took aim Friday at what he deemed the “weaponization of international law,” calling it a tool of the elite, and issued a stark warning to the International Criminal Court.

Rubio cautioned the ICC against “quoting laws to men with swords,” as he accused the Hague-based tribunal of trying to enforce rules that Washington does not recognize.

His remarks to the Federalist Society National Lawyers Convention came around a month after the United States announced new sanctions on the ICC, vowing to cripple its operations.

The court prosecutes individuals accused of the gravest atrocities and acts as a last resort when countries do not have adequate legal systems to ensure accountability.

The US signed the Rome Statute establishing the ICC but never ratified the treaty. Israel, Russia and China are also not ICC members.

Rubio’s keynote address at the conservative group, where he received a standing ovation, marks his first major US speech since the Republican Party’s sweeping losses in midterm elections earlier this month.

Rubio said Friday that international law had been invoked against “nearly every major foreign policy decision” of the Trump administration, from boat strikes in the Caribbean to the capture of Venezuelan leader Nicolas Maduro.

He charged that such law was not neutral, but has been an “instrument” for the global elite to advance their interests.

The top US diplomat previously said Washington would bar transactions with what he called a “rogue court,” stepping up a long-running campaign by US President Donald Trump’s government against the ICC.

Washington has vowed to dismantle the court, angered as judges issued an arrest warrant for Israel’s Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over alleged crimes in Gaza.

Rubio on Friday renewed criticism of the ICC, calling it accountable to no one although “armed with the power to investigate, to prosecute, to persecute and to jail our citizens, according to laws we neither consent nor control.”

He added: “If they’re foolish enough to try to enforce their paper decrees on Americans, our answer will probably be the same as the Roman general Pompey when he said to those who were trying to invoke their city’s charters against his legions.”

“He said: ‘Stop quoting laws to men with swords.'”

The venue of Rubio’s remarks, a gathering of the legal profession, could further speculation that he is looking beyond his foreign policy portfolio. Past presidential hopefuls have also addressed the conference.

Rubio is widely seen as a possible successor to Trump, although he has dismissed reports that he was planning to leave the administration to prepare for a 2028 election run.

World.title: Pak sending 'experienced' minister for Delhi event
World.content:
NEW DELHI:

announced on Saturday that it will participate in the inaugural Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held in New Delhi from November 20 to 22.

Prime Minister Narendra Modi had proposed the dialogue at the SCO summit in Tianjin in 2025.

The last visit by a Pakistani minister to India was in May 2023, when then Foreign Minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari travelled to Goa to attend a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. This will also be the first ministerial visit between the two countries since the Pahalgam terror attack last year.

Pakistanâs Ministry of Foreign Affairs said that Musadik Masood Malik, Federal Minister for Climate Change and Environmental Coordination, will lead the countryâs delegation to the dialogue.



India had invited culture minister Aurangzeb Khichi for the event. Musadik Masood Malik, federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, will lead the team. He however, is considered a more experienced minister in the Pakistan govt. "The event will bring together representatives from SCO member states to exchange views on issues related to civilisational dialogue and cultural understanding," said Pakistan in its announcement, adding that Islamabad remains committed to promoting dialogue among civilisations and fostering people-to-people ties within the SCO framework in a spirit of mutual respect.





After Bilawal's visit in 2023, external affairs minister S Jaishankar had visited Pakistan the next year, again for a meeting of SCO foreign ministers. On both occasions, there was no bilateral meeting between the ministers.

Even in the absence of any substantive bilateral engagement for over a decade, both countries have continued to interact within the Eurasian bloc which they both joined as full members in 2017.

World.title: Govt opens applications for companies to be consent managers under data law
World.content:
AI-generated image

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: Govt has opened applications for companies to become consent managers under India's data protection law. Once registered, these firms will be able to offer a website or app where users can review the permissions they have given to participating businesses and grant or withdraw consent.For users, the service could bring permissions from several businesses into one place. For instance, a user could review a data request from one company and withdraw an earlier permission given to another through the same app, if both businesses are on the platform.Consent managers will have to give users access to their consent history, including requests they declined and permissions they withdrew. Rules require firms to keep these records for at least seven years, put safeguards in place to prevent data breaches and avoid conflicts of interest with the businesses whose requests they handle.The registration framework under the Digital Personal Data Protection Act took effect on Nov 13. Electronics and IT secretary S Krishnan launched the application portal. Companies incorporated in India with a net worth of at least Rs 2 crore can apply. The Data Protection Board of India will assess whether applicants have the technical, operational and financial capacity to provide the service and publish a list of firms it registers.Govt is implementing the law in phases. Key provisions covering users' rights, companies' obligations and board's powers to conduct inquiries and impose penalties will take effect from May 13, 2027.

World.title: Magsaysay awardee in SC: 'Whistleblower Act in limbo for 12 yrs'
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Highlighting that there is no protection for honest govt officials and also private persons who face the music for exposing corruption by suffering frequent transfers and non-consequential postings, Magsaysay award winner and IFS officer Sanjeev Chaturvedi has moved the

for protection of whistleblowers, as the Centre has not notified the Whistleblower Protection Act despite it being passed by Parliament 12 years ago.

The officer, who himself is fighting multiple service litigations, has pleaded the apex court to intervene to protect honest officers, as the Whistle Blowers Protection Act, 2014, has remained a dead letter. There is a "structural vacuum," and the "inaction of the Executive is not merely a policy failure - it is a constitutionally impermissible abdication of a statutory obligation that strikes at the foundational rights of whistleblowers as well as citizens.



"

Referring to the turbulence in his own career, particularly the alleged vindictive approach of the Congress govt of Haryana between 2008 and 2012, when he was transferred 12 times in four years and was suspended multiple times, he said, "Continuity of institutional persecution in the absence of any protective framework has become systemic norm."

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

"The absence of the Act's operational framework means there is no single institutional mechanism to which a whistleblower in the petitioner's position can turn for protection, and there is no authority charged with the specific task of preventing and investigating retaliation," he said in an affidavit filed in SC.





"...The consequence of this executive inaction is that India has, for over 11 years, had no effective legislative framework for the protection of whistleblowers. During this period, countless potential disclosures of public corruption may have been suppressed, and brave individuals who did come forward have had no legal recourse."

The affidavit said India, being a signatory to the United Nations Convention Against Corruption, is required to adopt appropriate measures to protect witnesses, experts, victims, and reporting persons from potential retaliation or intimidation, and that not doing so amounts to a governance deficit.

World.title: Spate of ragging cases forces NMC to direct strict action
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A spate of disturbing ragging complaints by first-year MBBS students - ranging from being forced to imitate sexual acts, change clothes in front of others to late-night humiliation and social boycotts - has prompted National Medical Commission (NMC) to issue 18 notices or communications to 15 medical colleges between Oct 16 and Nov 11.

The complaints, received by NMC's anti-ragging cell, concern 14 colleges in Rajasthan and one in Karnataka. They allege physical and verbal abuse, sexual humiliation, coercive activities, restrictions on juniors' movement, and threats of academic retaliation.

The action comes amid a separate ragging case at Govt Medical College, Jalaun, UP, where videos of alleged harassment of junior students surfaced online in Oct.



The college initially suspended seven senior students for a week. Following a wider inquiry, 10 more were found involved, taking the total to 17 students, who were subsequently suspended for three months and fined Rs 25,000 each.

In most cases, NMC sought detailed action taken reports within 24 hours, directing colleges to identify those involved, preserve footage from CCTV cameras and digital evidence, conduct impartial inquiries and protect complainants from intimidation.





It has advised colleges to take the strictest action against students found guilty, including suspension or cancellation of their medical registration, an NMC official told TOI. Citing Gujarat as an example, he said some students' registrations had been suspended there.

He stressed that enforcement largely rested with state authorities and medical councils, adding lenient approach has often allowed offenders to escape action.

"NMC will support the harshest action, provided due process is followed," the official said.

Dr Lakshya Mittal, chairperson United Doctors Front said, "Young students enter medical colleges to build their future, not to face intimidation and exploitation. State govts must act immediately, order independent probes and hold college authorities accountable. No institution can be allowed to shield abuse in the name of tradition."

Some complaints describe particularly disturbing incidents. In Rajasthan's Banswara Govt Medical College, first-year students were allegedly forced to perform degrading postures, imitate sexual acts, dance to 'item' songs and change clothes in front of others. At Churu, complaints included forced haircuts, removal of clothing and sexual humiliation.

Other complaints cited coercive instructions in a "Personality Development Program" document at Sardar Patel Medical College, Bikaner, and alleged emotional and verbal abuse, with possible faculty involvement, at Karnataka's Ballari Medical College.

NMC has directed the colleges to conduct confidential student interviews, provide counselling and prevent retaliation against complainants. It has also sought details of the functioning of their anti-ragging committees and squads.

World.title: PM Modi, Nepal PM Balendra Shah likely to flag off Ayodhya-Janakpur train virtually on Nov 23
World.content:
LUCKNOW:

and his Nepalese counterpart Balendra Shah are likely to jointly inaugurate the new Ayodhya Dham-Janakpur Dham train service virtually from New Delhi on Nov 23, establishing a direct rail link between two prominent religious destinations associated with Lord Ram and Mata Sita.

The

has approved the weekly service connecting Ayodhya in Uttar Pradesh with Janakpur Dham in Nepal. Regular operations are expected to begin within a week of the proposed inauguration.

Railway officials said the train would operate with conventional Linke Hofmann Busch (LHB) coaches, comprising air-conditioned and sleeper accommodation, offering passengers an additional option for cross-border travel.



The train will cover approximately 604 km, connecting Janakpur Dham, regarded as the birthplace of Mata Sita, with Ayodhya, revered as the birthplace of Lord Ram.

âThe inaugural run will be from Ayodhya Dham on Nov 23, but the commercial service of the train will have Ayodhya Cantt as originating station,â said an official source of Lucknow division of Northern Railway.

According to the approved route, the train will have commercial stoppages at Jaynagar, Madhubani, Shisho, Sitamarhi, Raxaul, Narkatiaganj, Gorakhpur, Basti, Mankapur and Ayodhya Dham, besides its terminal stations.





The weekly service will originate from Janakpur Dham on Saturdays and from Ayodhya Cantt on Mondays. Detailed timings and fares are expected to be announced separately.

Railway officials said the service was primarily aimed at facilitating travel between the two religious centres, which attract pilgrims from India and Nepal throughout the year.

World.title: 'Completely false': NCP (SP) rejects merger buzz after Supriya Sule says talks ended with Ajit Pawar's death
World.content:
NEW DELHI: The Sharad Pawar-led Nationalist Congress Party (NCP-SP) on Saturday dismissed reports of a possible merger with the Ajit Pawar-led faction as "completely false", saying it had no plans to merge with any other political party.

NCP (SP) spokesperson Pravin Kunte Patil alleged that the reports were being deliberately circulated to divert public attention from pressing issues such as drought, inflation, unemployment, alleged vote theft and irregularities in Maharashtra Public Service Commission (MPSC) examinations.

"Our official stand is that those who wish to merge should join our party," Kunte Patil said, PTI reported.

His remarks came amid renewed speculation about a possible reunion between the two NCP factions: the one led by

and the other headed by Maharashtra Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar.



Earlier in the day, NCP (SP) working president

said discussions about a merger had ended for her following the death of her cousin, former NCP chief

. She also said she had received no communication from leaders of the other faction on the matter.

Speaking to reporters, Sule said merger discussions had taken place when Ajit Pawar was alive and that a date had even been decided. However, she said the discussions came to an end after his death.





"When my brother (then NCP chief Ajit Pawar) was alive, there were discussions about a merger. A date had also been decided. But the day my brother passed away, the merger issue came to a full stop for me and within our party," Sule said.

She said her party had neither made any announcement on a merger after Ajit Pawar's death nor responded to statements from the other faction.

"No spokesperson from our side has spoken on this issue in the last several months," she said.

Sule also said she had received no communication from the Ajit Pawar faction about a possible merger.

"Not a single phone call, WhatsApp message, SMS, letter or email has come to me from anyone in the Ajit Pawar faction regarding a merger. Nobody has contacted me. No one has met me regarding this," she added.

Sule said her relationship with Ajit Pawar was based on affection and not political considerations, adding that she did not see the point of discussing a merger after his death.

"For you, this may be a discussion or gossip. For us, these are emotions. Some things are done from the heart. My relationship with my brother was that of love and affection. He is no longer here. What is the point of discussing it now?" she said.

Asked whether talks could be held with Ajit Pawar's family, including his wife Sunetra Pawar, Sule said personal relationships should not be mixed with politics.

Sule also rejected speculation that the NCP (SP) could join the BJP-led National Democratic Alliance (NDA).

"There has been no discussion on joining the NDA. When there has been no beginning, where does the question of a full stop arise?" she said.

She declined to comment on statements made by senior leaders of the Ajit Pawar faction, including Chhagan Bhujbal, Sunil Tatkare, Praful Patel and Hasan Mushrif.

"These are senior leaders who have worked with my father. I am much younger than them in age and experience. The values my parents taught me are that one should not speak disrespectfully about people who are older or more experienced," she said.

Expressing frustration over repeated questions about a possible merger, Sule urged the media to focus on policy issues and hold political leaders accountable. She said she was "already bored with the subject".

"There are several important issues facing the country and the world. There are serious policy-making issues that need to be discussed. The FCRA Bill, One Nation, One Election and several other important issues are before us.

On her meetings with senior NCP leader Praful Patel, Sule said they were related to parliamentary committee work and had no political significance.

"I am a member of the Finance Committee and he is also involved in committee work. We also meet in connection with the JPC on the FCRA. These are institutional meetings, not political discussions," she added.

World.title: 'Introspect on your own prejudices': India hits back at US religious freedom panel over Sharjeel Imam post
World.content:
NEW DELHI: India's ambassador to US, Vinay Mohan Kwatra on Saturday hit back at the US Commission on International Religious Freedom (USCIRF), saying it had "no locus standi" to comment on the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.

His remarks came after the commission described jailed activist

as a person detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy.

In a strongly worded post on X, Kwatra rejected the commission's assessment and accused it of making partisan and ill-informed remarks about India's commitment to religious freedom and equal rights.

"USCRIF has no locus standi to sit in judgment over the constitutional rights of Indian citizens.



Its habitual partisan, ill-informed, and jaundiced assessments cannot diminish Indiaâs constitutional commitment to religious freedom and equal rights for all faiths," Kwatra said.

"India flourishes defying the agenda-driven partisan narratives of the USCIRF. Taking the same liberty that USCIRF so readily assumes, a word of advice: introspect on your own prejudices and stop lecturing others," he added.

USCIRF shared Imam's profile on X, describing him as "a Muslim man detained in India for his religious freedom advocacy".





The commission's post linked his detention to his advocacy for religious freedom, prompting a sharp response from the Indian envoy.

Imam, a former student activist was arrested in January 2020 in connection with protests against the Citizenship Amendment Act (CAA) held in December 2019 and January 2020, according to ANI. Authorities accused him of delivering speeches that allegedly incited communal violence.

In August 2020, he was charged in connection with FIR 59/2020, which relates to the alleged larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 North-East Delhi riots, according to ANI.

The case, being investigated by the

Special Cell, invokes provisions of the Indian Penal Code and the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). The charges include rioting, murder, promoting enmity, unlawful activities and alleged terrorist acts.

Imam was earlier granted interim bail from October 4 to October 10 to attend his cousin's wedding functions. The relief came with conditions barring him from using social media, interacting with media persons or meeting anyone other than family members, relatives and friends.

Established by the US government in 1998 after the inaction of the International Religious Freedom Act, the recommendations of USCIRF are non-binding on the US State Department.

World.title: U.S. must respect India’s right to defend itself, maintain zero tolerance towards terrorism: Blinken
World.content:
The U.S. must respect India's right to defend itself and should maintain a zero-tolerance policy towards terrorism, former U.S. Secretary of State Antony Blinken said on Saturday (November 14, 2026), while describing Washington’s ties with New Delhi and Islamabad as “fundamentally different".

“India is a global force,” Mr. Blinken said, adding that the relationship and shared interests between Washington and New Delhi were “really global in nature”.

In contrast, the U.S. relationship with Pakistan is “regional," he said during a conversation with Jawed Ashraf, chairman of the India Trade Promotion Organisation, at a summit in New Delhi.

“The relations with Pakistan are regional, and there are still going to be important areas where we need to do things with them, particularly, for example, when it comes to counter-terrorism, but these are fundamentally different relationships,” he said.

“We have to have a zero-tolerance policy for terrorism. Period. And that means that we have to have respect for India's right to defend itself,” he added.

Mr. Blinken said the U.S. approach must include support for India’s efforts to respond to attacks as well as diplomatic efforts to prevent an escalation between New Delhi and Islamabad, the two nuclear-armed neighbours.

He added that efforts to prevent escalation were important given the destructive potential of the weapons both countries possess.

Reflecting on Washington's past engagement with Islamabad, Mr. Blinken said U.S. strategic interests during the Cold War and the war in Afghanistan may have led successive administrations to be less critical of Pakistan's civil-military establishment.

“And there's certainly an opportunity for the United States to do more,” he added.

On India-U.S. relations, Mr. Blinken described the transformation in ties over the past few decades as a shift from estrangement to a strategic partnership, underpinned by shared interests and people-to-people connections.

“We moved from estrangement to a genuine and, in some ways, unique partnership, built on a convergence of strategic interests. Of course, it is also underpinned by the profound people-to-people connections between our societies,” he said.

He identified cooperation in emerging technologies as an important area for the two countries, pointing to collaboration in space, quantum technology and artificial intelligence.

“The next step is tech cooperation, our ability to work in space, tech, quantum, and artificial intelligence,” he said.

On India’s relations with Russia, Mr. Blinken acknowledged the partnership's historical depth and said Washington did not expect New Delhi to sever those ties.

“There will be places where we don't have the same perspectives. For Russia, we understand there is deep history between India and Russia. So, we don't want them to end it,” he said.

Mr. Blinken, who served as the 71st Secretary of State from 2021 to 2025 under then-President Joe Biden, said the world was at a profound inflection point, citing rapid technological change, inequality and shifting power.

“The speed and profundity of change is beyond anything we've seen, certainly in my lifetime,” he said, noting that ChatGPT, an Artificial Intelligence (AI) chatbot, took one month to reach 50 million users, compared with 75 years for the telephone.

He said the private sector increasingly drove technological change, while governments struggled to keep pace. Growing inequalities had fuelled a sense among younger people that they were being “left out, left behind", he said.

Mr. Blinken warned that the U.S. risked weakening its strength by damaging cooperation between the government, universities and research institutions, and by becoming less welcoming to skilled people from abroad.

“The biggest danger I think we face is a huge self-inflicted wound,” he said.

On U.S. domestic politics, Mr. Blinken said the recent midterm results went beyond the usual setback for the party of a sitting President. He attributed the outcome partly to frustration over the cost of living and concerns about corruption.

In the November 3 midterm elections, the Democratic Party won majorities in both the House of Representatives and the Senate, shifting control of the US Congress away from Republicans.

Mr. Blinken described the U.S.-Israeli military campaign against Iran, launched in February by President Donald Trump, as “a war of choice" and said the first Trump administration’s withdrawal from the 2015 nuclear agreement with Tehran had contributed to the crisis.

He said the agreement, signed in 2015 and formally known as the Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA), required Iran to ship out 97% of its enriched uranium and placed limits on its centrifuges, while allowing extensive inspections.

After the U.S. withdrawal from JCPOA in 2018, Iran accelerated its nuclear programme, Blinken added, saying the ongoing military action would not resolve the issue.

“It is very hard to try to force this Iranian regime to capitulate; it is possible to get it to negotiate. And these are very different things,” he said.

He called for an “off-ramp” to the conflict, warning that escalation could involve attacks on regional infrastructure, US bases and partner countries.

The Strait of Hormuz, he said, had become a major challenge for global energy supplies after not being a problem before the war. Since February, Iran has repeatedly restricted access to the narrow chokepoint, one of the world's busiest oil shipping channels.

On the wider West Asia conflict, Mr. Blinken said a lasting settlement required resolving the Palestinian question and establishing a sovereign Palestinian state alongside a secure Israel.

“There are seven million Jews in Israel. There are seven million Arabs and Palestinians between Israel proper, the West Bank and Gaza. No one is going anywhere despite what extremists on both sides would like to see happen," he said.

"The solution remains, I fully believe, even though this is not a popular view, a secure Israel and a sovereign state of Palestine," he added.

World.title: China border has become 'more alive,' India enhancing frontier infrastructure: Jaishankar
World.content:
India's border with China has become "more alive" and requires a much greater commitment of Indian troops on a sustained basis, External Affairs Minister S. Jaishankar said on Saturday (November 14, 2026) as he listed New Delhi's policy approach to enhance infrastructure along the frontier.

Mr. Jaishankar also said that India has bolstered its military capabilities along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) since the deadly clashes in Eastern Ladakh's Galwan Valley in 2020.

His remarks at an interactive session at the HT Leadership Summit came amid ongoing efforts by New Delhi and Beijing to normalise their relations that came under severe strain following the over four-year border face-off in Eastern Ladakh.

"Just think about the last few years. How often do you now read - a new tunnel has been built, some new bridge has been built, another airfield has been commissioned. You're getting this news with greater and greater frequency," he said.

"What has happened today is the border with China has become more alive in a way. It has required a much greater commitment of troops on a sustained basis."

"The fact is that the work we had already done allowed that kind of numbers to be deployed out there, and the work we continue to do will maintain those numbers," he said.

After over four years of frosty ties over the eastern Ladakh military standoff, India and China began to repair relations following a meeting between Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Chinese President Xi Jinping in the Russian city of Kazan in October 2024 that took place after the face-off ended.

The talks between Mr. Modi and Mr. Xi covered a range of issues, including reducing their trade deficit, tackling challenges like terrorism and ensuring fair trade in multilateral platforms.

"I would say when it comes to the border, I would honestly make this point, and I think there's a lot of data and evidence to back it up, which is that the border infrastructure was really neglected till about a decade ago. I mean, people spoke about it, people drew up plan," Mr. Jaishankar said.

"If you actually go on the ground and see year-by-year how many kilometres of roads, what was the tunnelling, what was the positioning, I think anybody, and certainly anybody associated with the armed forces dealing with that sector knows the truth," he noted.

Mr. Jaishankar added: "It's really been in the last decade that that kind of attention, resources, policy push has been given."

The External Affairs Minister said India's capability to "deploy" its troops on that border has seen "a very marked" improvement.

Mr. Jaishankar also responded to a question on views about economic asymmetry between the two countries.

"On the economic side, the 1960s, 1970s, 1980s, this was the time the world was industrialising, developing countries were industrialising. Remember, when around the time when Rajiv Gandhi went to China in 1988, the Indian and Chinese economies were about the same size," he said.

"But the fact was that China, in the 1980s particularly, made a huge push towards modernisation and industrialisation. I'm sorry to say India in the 1980s simply missed the bus. Now in the 1990s, we did some corrections, reforms, but we did not carry through the reforms sector by sector and keep building and raising it," he said.

"I don't want you to think of it as a political point." The External Affairs Minister listed efforts by the Modi government in the areas of manufacturing and industrialisation.

"The fact is, there were decades where we missed out; now we have to play catch up; you can't play catch up by following the same track. You have to do leap-frogging. We'll have to build up our particular strengths to deal with this asymmetry issue."

"In asymmetry, you don't go toe-to-toe on every issue. You pick the issues where you feel you have the ability to make a big change. That's really what we think we're doing right now," he said.

World.title: Bomb rips through Damascus suburb; killing 2, including child
World.content:
An explosive device placed inside a car in a suburb of Syria’s capital exploded on Saturday evening (November 15, 2026), killing two people and wounding at least one, state TV and the Interior Ministry said.

The explosion took place in the southern Damascus suburb of Jaramana near a factory where batteries are produced, state TV said. It said two people were killed and two were wounded, without giving further details.

The Interior Ministry said the dead included a child, adding that one person was wounded. It said security forces cordoned off the area and started an investigation.

Several explosions have taken place in Damascus and its suburbs in recent months as the country’s security remains fragile nearly two years after five decades of Assad family rule ended in December 2024. Militants stormed the capital and removed then-President Bashar Assad from power.

Jaramana is home to a large community of the Druze religious minority. The suburb has faced tensions between some members of the community and Sunni Muslim Syrians supportive of the country’s current Islamist-led government.

World.title: Drought-stricken Beed: Land of parched fields and broken promises
World.content:
The cotton plants are green, but the bolls are missing. Across the Chauhan family’s four-acre field in Majalgaon in Maharashtra’s Beed district, the plants stand stunted, their promise of a harvest withered by the absence of rain. What should have been a season of cotton picking has become a search for the few bolls the drought has spared.

Under the relentless October sun, Vanita Chauhan bends over the plants, picking the little cotton she can find. A tattered towel covers her head, shielding her from the scorching heat. Her full-sleeved shirt is buttoned up to her neck, while the red pallu of her sari is tied around her arm and neck, fashioned into an improvised pouch. She drops each cotton boll into it before moving hurriedly to the next plant.

World.title: SpaceX’s Starship returns from orbit and is captured by launch pad arms in a dramatic first
World.content:
SpaceX’s Starship made a triumphant return to Earth on Saturday (November 14, 2026), caught in midair by giant mechanical arms where its journey began 22 hours earlier.

It was the grand finale that Elon Musk and his team hoped for — the first-ever capture of a Starship flying back from space. But with the first-stage booster exploding shortly after Friday’s liftoff from Texas, the company fell short of its desired double catch.

Wreckage remained in the Gulf of Mexico, cordoned off by buoys, as the stainless steel, bullet-shaped spacecraft lowered itself upright at the launch pad.

“Can you believe it?” shouted SpaceX commentator Dan Huot.

SpaceX officials said Saturday’s catch demonstrates the full reusability of Starship, intended for moon and Mars travel. Although Friday’s booster recovery failed, the company had already made three previous booster catches, validating the technique.
